# Which webhook events does RevenueDot send?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md
Description: Every webhook event type RevenueDot sends, when each fires, its fields and a real example payload, plus the signature header and retry rules.

RevenueDot POSTs one JSON event per request to each matching webhook: `{ "api_version": "1.0", "event": { ... } }`. The payload matches RevenueCat's webhook format field for field, so existing handlers keep working. Set up, verify and test webhooks with the [webhooks guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/webhooks.md).

- **Headers:** `Content-Type: application/json`, `User-Agent: RevenueDot-Webhooks/1.0`, `X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`, and your `Authorization` header when you set one.
- **Delivery:** only HTTP 200 counts. Anything else, or no answer within 60 seconds, is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes, then marked failed. Deliveries can repeat: deduplicate on `event.id`.
- **Examples:** recorded from a RevenueDot server on 2026-09-30 with Test Store purchases. Events that the Test Store cannot produce (pause, product change, extension, refund reversal, uncancellation, price consent) show the same builder's output with App Store or Google Play values. `PURCHASE_REDEEMED` and the funnel events show the builder's output for a web checkout on a test-mode Stripe account.

| Event | When it is sent |
|---|---|
| [`INITIAL_PURCHASE`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#initial_purchase) | The first purchase of a subscription, including a free trial start. |
| [`RENEWAL`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#renewal) | A new paid period: a renewal, a trial converting (`is_trial_conversion: true`), a lapsed customer resubscribing, or a recovered billing issue. |
| [`CANCELLATION`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#cancellation) | Auto-renew was turned off, or the purchase was refunded. Access continues to `expiration_at_ms` unless it was a refund. A refund has `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price. |
| [`UNCANCELLATION`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#uncancellation) | Auto-renew was turned back on before the subscription expired. |
| [`NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#non_renewing_purchase) | A one-time purchase: consumable, non-consumable or lifetime. |
| [`SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#subscription_paused) | A Google Play subscription is scheduled to pause. It will not renew at the end of the period. |
| [`EXPIRATION`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#expiration) | Access ended: the period ran out, billing retry gave up or the subscription paused. |
| [`BILLING_ISSUE`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#billing_issue) | A renewal charge failed. The store retries; access may continue in a grace period. |
| [`PRODUCT_CHANGE`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#product_change) | The customer changed product: an upgrade now, or a downgrade or crossgrade scheduled for the next renewal. `product_id` is the old product. |
| [`SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#subscription_extended) | The current period got longer without a new payment: an App Store renewal extension or a Google Play deferral. |
| [`REFUND_REVERSED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#refund_reversed) | A refund was reversed and access is back. |
| [`PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_REQUIRED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#price_increase_consent_required) | The store asks the customer to accept a price increase. |
| [`PRICE_INCREASE_CONSENT_APPROVED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#price_increase_consent_approved) | The customer accepted the price increase. |
| [`TRANSFER`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#transfer) | A purchase moved to another customer because that customer restored it (transfer behaviour `transfer` or `transfer_if_no_active`). |
| [`VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#virtual_currency_transaction) | An in-app currency was credited because a purchase of a granting product was recorded (`source: in_app_purchase`), or because a rewarded ad was verified and a reward rule granted currency (`source: ad_reward`, a RevenueDot extension; `product_id` and `store` are null and `transaction_id` is the ad network's transaction id). Not sent for adjustments made through the API. |
| [`EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#experiment_enrollment) | A customer joined an offering experiment: the first offerings request that enrolled them. Its `app_user_id` is the id that asked for offerings. Sent once per customer and experiment, as a production event with no app, so a webhook set to sandbox only or to one app does not get it. See [Experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md#webhooks). |
| [`SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#subscriber_alias) | A new app user id joined an existing customer: `logIn` onto an anonymous customer, `logIn` that merged an anonymous customer into an existing one, Android's alias call, or a restore that merged two customers. RevenueCat deprecated this event and sends it only to older projects, so RevenueDot delivers it only to webhooks whose `event_types` filter names `subscriber_alias`; it always appears in the customer's event history. |
| [`PURCHASE_REDEEMED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#purchase_redeemed) | A web purchase was redeemed in the app through a redemption link (`POST /v1/subscribers/redeem_purchase`): the anonymous customer who paid on the web was merged into the app user. Fields follow RevenueCat's sample; `app_user_id` is added so analytics tools know who it is. See [Redemption links](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/redemption-links.md). |
| [`FUNNEL_VIEWED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#funnel_viewed) | RevenueDot type. A visitor opened a published funnel. Opt-in: sent only to webhooks and integrations whose `event_types` names `funnel_viewed`. `app_user_id` is null unless the page URL had `?app_user_id=`. See [Funnels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/funnels.md). |
| [`FUNNEL_STEP_COMPLETED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#funnel_step_completed) | RevenueDot type. A visitor finished a funnel step, with the answer for a question (an email step's answer is `provided`, never the address). Opt-in: `funnel_step_completed`. |
| [`FUNNEL_PURCHASE`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#funnel_purchase) | RevenueDot type. A funnel's checkout was paid. `app_user_id` is the buyer's (anonymous unless the page had one) and `product_id` the Stripe price. Opt-in: `funnel_purchase`. |
| [`PAYWALL_IMPRESSION`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_impression) | A paywall was shown (RevenueDot type; the SDK reports it to `POST /v1/events`). Opt-in: sent only to webhooks and integrations whose `event_types` names `paywall_impression`. RevenueCat sends paywall events to Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog and Segment only, not to webhooks. See [Integrations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/integrations.md#paywall-events). |
| [`PAYWALL_CLOSE`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_close) | The customer closed a paywall. Opt-in: `paywall_close`. |
| [`PAYWALL_CANCEL`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_cancel) | The customer dismissed the store's payment sheet on a paywall. Opt-in: `paywall_cancel`. |
| [`PAYWALL_EXIT_OFFER`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_exit_offer) | An exit offer was shown when the customer left a paywall. Opt-in: `paywall_exit_offer`. |
| [`PAYWALL_COMPONENT_INTERACTED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_component_interacted) | The customer changed a paywall control: a tab, package, button or sheet. Opt-in: `paywall_component_interacted`. |
| [`PAYWALL_PURCHASE_INITIATED`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_purchase_initiated) | The customer started a purchase from a paywall. A RevenueDot addition: RevenueCat does not forward it. Opt-in: `paywall_purchase_initiated`. |
| [`PAYWALL_PURCHASE_ERROR`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#paywall_purchase_error) | A purchase started from a paywall failed. A RevenueDot addition: RevenueCat does not forward it. Opt-in: `paywall_purchase_error`. |
| [`TEST`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/webhook-events.md#test) | Sent by the dashboard's "Send test event" or `POST .../integrations/webhooks/{id}/test`. Shaped like a purchase, for no real customer, so it never carries `experiments`. |

Accepted in a webhook's `event_types` filter but never sent, because RevenueDot never has the fact behind them: `TEMPORARY_ENTITLEMENT_GRANT` (RevenueDot never grants access it has not verified with the store; during a store outage the SDK keeps the purchase and grants access on the device from the [offline entitlement mapping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/offline-entitlements.md)) and `INVOICE_ISSUANCE` (only RevenueCat Billing issues invoices). That makes 19 of RevenueCat's 21 event types sent. `SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS` and RevenueDot's three funnel types (`FUNNEL_VIEWED`, `FUNNEL_STEP_COMPLETED`, `FUNNEL_PURCHASE`) are opt-in: they go only to webhooks whose filter names them. So are the seven paywall types the SDKs report (`PAYWALL_IMPRESSION`, `PAYWALL_CLOSE`, `PAYWALL_CANCEL`, `PAYWALL_EXIT_OFFER`, `PAYWALL_COMPONENT_INTERACTED`, `PAYWALL_PURCHASE_INITIATED`, `PAYWALL_PURCHASE_ERROR`); RevenueCat sends paywall events to analytics integrations only, not to webhooks.

## INITIAL_PURCHASE

The first purchase of a subscription, including a free trial start.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `product_id` | string | Store product id. For PRODUCT_CHANGE, the product the customer changed from. |
| `period_type` | `NORMAL`, `TRIAL`, `INTRO`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `PREPAID` |  |
| `purchased_at_ms` | integer | Start of the period. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `expiration_at_ms` | integer or null | End of the period, or null for lifetime. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` |  |
| `entitlement_id` | null | Always null (deprecated in RevenueCat's payload). |
| `entitlement_ids` | array of string | Lookup keys of the entitlements the product unlocks, or null. |
| `presented_offering_id` | string or null | Offering the purchase was made from, when the SDK sent it. |
| `transaction_id` | string or null | Store transaction id of this period. |
| `original_transaction_id` | string or null | First transaction id of the subscription. |
| `is_family_share` | boolean |  |
| `country_code` | string or null | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. |
| `currency` | string or null | ISO 4217. |
| `price` | number or null | USD. Money moved only on INITIAL_PURCHASE, RENEWAL, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE, REFUND_REVERSED and refunds (negative); 0 on other events. |
| `price_in_purchased_currency` | number or null | Same as price, in `currency`. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |
| `store` | `APP_STORE`, `MAC_APP_STORE`, `PLAY_STORE`, `AMAZON`, `STRIPE`, `RC_BILLING`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `TEST_STORE`, `PADDLE`, `ROKU`, `EXTERNAL` |  |
| `takehome_percentage` | number | 1 minus the estimated store commission. |
| `tax_percentage` | number | Always 0 today. |
| `commission_percentage` | number | Estimated store commission (0.3 for App Store and Google Play, 0 for Test Store). |
| `offer_code` | string or null | The App Store or Google Play offer id of this period (a promotional offer, offer code, win-back offer or Google offer), or null. See [Win-back offers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/win-back-offers.md). |
| `experiments` | array of object | Every offering experiment the customer joined. Left out when there are none. See [Experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md#webhooks). |
| `experiments[].experiment_id` | string |  |
| `experiments[].experiment_variant` | `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` |  |
| `experiments[].enrolled_at_ms` | integer | Epoch milliseconds. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "id": "66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2",
    "type": "INITIAL_PURCHASE",
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790800914034,
    "app_id": "appvnrm0a5h",
    "app_user_id": "user_1",
    "original_app_user_id": "user_1",
    "aliases": [
      "user_1"
    ],
    "product_id": "pro_monthly",
    "period_type": "NORMAL",
    "purchased_at_ms": 1790800914000,
    "expiration_at_ms": 1793392914000,
    "environment": "SANDBOX",
    "entitlement_id": null,
    "entitlement_ids": [
      "pro"
    ],
    "presented_offering_id": "default",
    "transaction_id": "test_1790800914000_quickstart",
    "original_transaction_id": "test_1790800914000_quickstart",
    "is_family_share": false,
    "country_code": null,
    "currency": "USD",
    "price": 9.99,
    "price_in_purchased_currency": 9.99,
    "subscriber_attributes": {},
    "store": "TEST_STORE",
    "takehome_percentage": 1,
    "tax_percentage": 0,
    "commission_percentage": 0,
    "offer_code": null
  }
}
```

## RENEWAL

A new paid period: a renewal, a trial converting (`is_trial_conversion: true`), a lapsed customer resubscribing, or a recovered billing issue.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `product_id` | string | Store product id. For PRODUCT_CHANGE, the product the customer changed from. |
| `period_type` | `NORMAL`, `TRIAL`, `INTRO`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `PREPAID` |  |
| `purchased_at_ms` | integer | Start of the period. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `expiration_at_ms` | integer or null | End of the period, or null for lifetime. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` |  |
| `entitlement_id` | null | Always null (deprecated in RevenueCat's payload). |
| `entitlement_ids` | array of string | Lookup keys of the entitlements the product unlocks, or null. |
| `presented_offering_id` | string or null | Offering the purchase was made from, when the SDK sent it. |
| `transaction_id` | string or null | Store transaction id of this period. |
| `original_transaction_id` | string or null | First transaction id of the subscription. |
| `is_family_share` | boolean |  |
| `country_code` | string or null | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. |
| `currency` | string or null | ISO 4217. |
| `price` | number or null | USD. Money moved only on INITIAL_PURCHASE, RENEWAL, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE, REFUND_REVERSED and refunds (negative); 0 on other events. |
| `price_in_purchased_currency` | number or null | Same as price, in `currency`. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |
| `store` | `APP_STORE`, `MAC_APP_STORE`, `PLAY_STORE`, `AMAZON`, `STRIPE`, `RC_BILLING`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `TEST_STORE`, `PADDLE`, `ROKU`, `EXTERNAL` |  |
| `takehome_percentage` | number | 1 minus the estimated store commission. |
| `tax_percentage` | number | Always 0 today. |

| `experiments[].experiment_id` | string |  |
| `experiments[].experiment_variant` | `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` |  |
| `experiments[].enrolled_at_ms` | integer | Epoch milliseconds. |
| `is_trial_conversion` | boolean | True for the first paid period after a free trial. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "id": "96E753E0-4DEC-4F9B-ABC5-55FBC363769A",
    "type": "RENEWAL",

    "entitlement_id": null,
    "entitlement_ids": [
      "pro"
    ],
    "presented_offering_id": null,
    "transaction_id": "test_1790800923895_c8ba6a2d-5f87-4e08-bb4b-f880624bcd6c..1",
    "original_transaction_id": "test_1790800923895_c8ba6a2d-5f87-4e08-bb4b-f880624bcd6c",
    "is_family_share": false,
    "country_code": null,
    "currency": "USD",
    "price": 9.99,
    "price_in_purchased_currency": 9.99,
    "subscriber_attributes": {},

  }
```

## CANCELLATION

Auto-renew was turned off, or the purchase was refunded. Access continues to `expiration_at_ms` unless it was a refund. A refund has `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `product_id` | string | Store product id. For PRODUCT_CHANGE, the product the customer changed from. |
| `period_type` | `NORMAL`, `TRIAL`, `INTRO`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `PREPAID` |  |
| `purchased_at_ms` | integer | Start of the period. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `expiration_at_ms` | integer or null | End of the period, or null for lifetime. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` |  |
| `entitlement_id` | null | Always null (deprecated in RevenueCat's payload). |
| `entitlement_ids` | array of string | Lookup keys of the entitlements the product unlocks, or null. |
| `presented_offering_id` | string or null | Offering the purchase was made from, when the SDK sent it. |
| `transaction_id` | string or null | Store transaction id of this period. |
| `original_transaction_id` | string or null | First transaction id of the subscription. |
| `is_family_share` | boolean |  |
| `country_code` | string or null | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. |
| `currency` | string or null | ISO 4217. |
| `price` | number or null | USD. Money moved only on INITIAL_PURCHASE, RENEWAL, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE, REFUND_REVERSED and refunds (negative); 0 on other events. |
| `price_in_purchased_currency` | number or null | Same as price, in `currency`. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |
| `store` | `APP_STORE`, `MAC_APP_STORE`, `PLAY_STORE`, `AMAZON`, `STRIPE`, `RC_BILLING`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `TEST_STORE`, `PADDLE`, `ROKU`, `EXTERNAL` |  |
| `takehome_percentage` | number | 1 minus the estimated store commission. |
| `tax_percentage` | number | Always 0 today. |

| `experiments` | array of object | Every offering experiment the customer joined. Left out when there are none. See [Experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md#webhooks). |
| `experiments[].experiment_id` | string |  |
| `experiments[].experiment_variant` | `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` |  |
| `experiments[].enrolled_at_ms` | integer | Epoch milliseconds. |
| `cancel_reason` | `UNSUBSCRIBE`, `BILLING_ERROR`, `DEVELOPER_INITIATED`, `PRICE_INCREASE`, `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`, `UNKNOWN` |  |

## VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION

An in-app currency was credited because a purchase of a granting product was recorded (`source: in_app_purchase`), or because a rewarded ad was verified and a reward rule granted currency (`source: ad_reward`, a RevenueDot extension; `product_id` and `store` are null and `transaction_id` is the ad network's transaction id). Not sent for adjustments made through the API.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `store` | `APP_STORE`, `MAC_APP_STORE`, `PLAY_STORE`, `AMAZON`, `STRIPE`, `RC_BILLING`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `TEST_STORE`, `PADDLE`, `ROKU`, `EXTERNAL`, null | Null for an ad reward. |
| `adjustments` | array of object |  |
| `adjustments[].amount` | integer | Credited amount. |
| `adjustments[].currency` | object |  |
| `product_id` | string or null | The granting product, or null for an ad reward. |
| `product_display_name` | string or null | The product's display name, or null for an ad reward. |
| `purchase_environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` |  |
| `source` | `in_app_purchase`, `ad_reward` | `ad_reward` is a RevenueDot extension: RevenueCat documents no source value for rewarded ads. |
| `transaction_id` | string or null | Store transaction id of this period. |
| `virtual_currency_transaction_id` | string | Starts with vatx. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "adjustments": [
      {

        }

    ],
    "app_id": "appe8dyp6dl",
    "app_user_id": "user_1",
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790800914012,
    "product_display_name": "100 coins",
    "product_id": "coins_100",
    "purchase_environment": "PRODUCTION",
    "source": "in_app_purchase",
    "store": "APP_STORE",
    "subscriber_attributes": {
      "$email": {
        "updated_at_ms": 1790800900000,
        "value": "ana@example.com"
      }
    },
    "transaction_id": "2000000123456789",
    "virtual_currency_transaction_id": "vatx1a2b3c4d5e6f7g",
    "type": "VIRTUAL_CURRENCY_TRANSACTION",

  }
```

## EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT

A customer joined an offering experiment: the first offerings request that enrolled them. Its `app_user_id` is the id that asked for offerings. Sent once per customer and experiment, as a production event with no app, so a webhook set to sandbox only or to one app does not get it. See [Experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md#webhooks).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `experiment_id` | string |  |
| `experiment_variant` | `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` | `a` is the control; `b`, `c` and `d` are treatments. |
| `offering_id` | string or null | The variant's offering identifier. |
| `experiment_enrolled_at_ms` | integer | Epoch milliseconds. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790800914012,
    "app_user_id": "$RCAnonymousID:12345678123412341234123456789123",
    "aliases": [
      "$RCAnonymousID:12345678123412341234123456789123"
    ],
    "original_app_user_id": "$RCAnonymousID:12345678123412341234123456789123",
    "experiment_id": "prexpca1234ab",
    "experiment_variant": "b",
    "offering_id": "promo",
    "experiment_enrolled_at_ms": 1790800914012,
    "type": "EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT",
    "id": "0F1E2D3C-4B5A-4978-8695-A4B3C2D1E0F9"
  }
}
```

## SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS

A new app user id joined an existing customer: `logIn` onto an anonymous customer, `logIn` that merged an anonymous customer into an existing one, Android's alias call, or a restore that merged two customers. RevenueCat deprecated this event and sends it only to older projects, so RevenueDot delivers it only to webhooks whose `event_types` filter names `subscriber_alias`; it always appears in the customer's event history.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the app uses now. |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |
| `experiments` | array of object | Every offering experiment the customer joined. Left out when there are none. See [Experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md#webhooks). |
| `experiments[].experiment_id` | string |  |
| `experiments[].experiment_variant` | `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` |  |
| `experiments[].enrolled_at_ms` | integer | Epoch milliseconds. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "aliases": [
      "$RCAnonymousID:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
      "user_1"
    ],
    "app_id": "appvnrm0a5h",
    "app_user_id": "user_1",
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790800925011,
    "original_app_user_id": "$RCAnonymousID:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef",
    "subscriber_attributes": {
      "$email": {
        "value": "ana@example.com",
        "updated_at_ms": 1790800901000
      }
    },
    "type": "SUBSCRIBER_ALIAS",

  }
}
```

## PURCHASE_REDEEMED

A web purchase was redeemed in the app through a redemption link (`POST /v1/subscribers/redeem_purchase`): the anonymous customer who paid on the web was merged into the app user. Fields follow RevenueCat's sample; `app_user_id` is added so analytics tools know who it is. See [Redemption links](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/redemption-links.md).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | The Stripe app the purchase was made through. |
| `store` | `STRIPE` |  |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` |  |
| `redeemed_from` | array of string | The anonymous web buyer's app user id. |
| `redeemed_by` | array of string | The app user id that redeemed it. |
| `redemption_outcome` | `alias` | The web customer was merged into the app user. |
| `redemption_platform` | string or null | From the SDK's X-Platform header: ios, android, web ... |
| `product_id` | string or null | The web product's store identifier (the Stripe price id). |
| `entitlement_ids` | array of string | Entitlements the product unlocks, or null. |
| `workflow_id` | string or null | The funnel id when the purchase came from a funnel, else null. |
| `workflow_step_id` | null |  |
| `trace_id` | string | The web checkout id (wco_...). |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id that redeemed it. A RevenueDot addition to RevenueCat's sample. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "app_id": "appstrp8k2m9q4",
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790801342625,
    "id": "5B2E8C1D-9F3A-4E7B-A6C0-1D2E3F4A5B6C",
    "store": "STRIPE",
    "environment": "SANDBOX",
    "redeemed_from": [
      "$RCAnonymousID:7c1e9b2f4a6d48e3b05f9a8c2d1e3f47"
    ],
    "redeemed_by": [
      "user_1"
    ],
    "redemption_outcome": "alias",
    "redemption_platform": "ios",
    "product_id": "price_1QxR2nKc8Hn4AbCd",
    "entitlement_ids": [
      "pro"
    ],
    "workflow_id": "fnl_7q2k9m4x1z8c",
    "workflow_step_id": null,
    "trace_id": "wco_8k2m9q4x7a1b3c5d",
    "app_user_id": "user_1",
    "type": "PURCHASE_REDEEMED"
  }
}
```

## FUNNEL_VIEWED

RevenueDot type. A visitor opened a published funnel. Opt-in: sent only to webhooks and integrations whose `event_types` names `funnel_viewed`. `app_user_id` is null unless the page URL had `?app_user_id=`. See [Funnels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/funnels.md).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string or null | The funnel's Stripe app. |
| `app_user_id` | string or null | The visitor's app user id, when known. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` | SANDBOX when the Stripe app uses a test-mode key. |
| `store` | `STRIPE` |  |
| `funnel_id` | string |  |
| `funnel_name` | string |  |
| `funnel_slug` | string |  |
| `session_id` | string | The page session; one per visit. |
| `step_id` | string or null |  |
| `step_type` | `question`, `info`, `email`, `paywall`, `success`, null |  |
| `step_index` | integer or null | 0-based position of the step. |
| `answer` | string or array of string or null | FUNNEL_STEP_COMPLETED of a question: the answer, or a list for multiple choice. Otherwise null. |
| `product_id` | string | FUNNEL_PURCHASE only: the Stripe price id. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object | Always empty. |
| `revenue_usd` | number | FUNNEL_PURCHASE only: what the buyer paid, in US dollars. |
| `currency` | `USD` | FUNNEL_PURCHASE only: the currency of `revenue_usd`. |
| `click_ids` | object | The ad click ids from the landing page's URL, when it had any. Checkouts and purchases take them from the visit's first page view while an integration asks for funnel events. |
| `click_ids.fbclid` | string |  |
| `click_ids.gclid` | string |  |
| `click_ids.gbraid` | string |  |
| `click_ids.wbraid` | string |  |
| `click_ids.ttclid` | string |  |
| `click_ids.msclkid` | string |  |
| `client_ip` | string | The visitor's IP address, for Meta and Branch: only while one of them (enabled) has a funnel event type in its filter; otherwise no visitor IP is stored. Deleted after 7 days. Never for a visitor with Global Privacy Control on. |
| `client_user_agent` | string | The visitor's browser user agent. Same conditions as `client_ip`. |
| `page_url` | string | The funnel page's address, without its query. While any enabled integration (not a webhook) has a funnel event type in its filter; not for a visitor with Global Privacy Control on. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "id": "A1C3E5F7-2B4D-4F6A-8C0E-1A3C5E7F9B2D",
    "type": "FUNNEL_VIEWED",
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790800914034,
    "app_id": "appstrp8k2m9q4",
    "environment": "SANDBOX",
    "store": "STRIPE",
    "funnel_id": "fnl_7q2k9m4x1z8c",
    "funnel_name": "Focus quiz",
    "funnel_slug": "focus-quiz",
    "session_id": "3f9c2a7b1e8d4c6a9b0f1e2d3c4b5a69",
    "app_user_id": null,
    "aliases": [],
    "step_id": null,
    "step_type": null,
    "step_index": null,
    "answer": null,
    "utm_source": "tiktok",
    "utm_campaign": "fall",
    "subscriber_attributes": {},
    "click_ids": {
      "fbclid": "IwAR2xQ9kM"
    }
  }
}
```

## PAYWALL_IMPRESSION

A paywall was shown (RevenueDot type; the SDK reports it to `POST /v1/events`). Opt-in: sent only to webhooks and integrations whose `event_types` names `paywall_impression`. RevenueCat sends paywall events to Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog and Segment only, not to webhooks. See [Integrations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/integrations.md#paywall-events).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | A UUID derived from the project and the SDK's event id, so a batch the SDK sends again is not delivered twice. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` | SANDBOX for TestFlight, Xcode and Test Store builds. |
| `store` | string | The app's store: APP_STORE, PLAY_STORE, TEST_STORE ... |
| `paywall_id` | string | The paywall's id. |
| `paywall_name` | string | The paywall's name, when it has one. |
| `paywall_revision` | integer |  |
| `offering_id` | string |  |
| `session_id` | string | One per time the paywall is shown. |
| `display_mode` | string | full_screen, sheet, condensed_footer ... |
| `dark_mode` | boolean |  |
| `locale` | string |  |
| `source` | string |  |
| `placement_identifier` | string |  |
| `targeting_revision` | integer |  |
| `targeting_rule_id` | string |  |
| `workflow_id` | string |  |
| `exit_offer_type` | string | PAYWALL_EXIT_OFFER: `dismiss`. |
| `exit_offering_id` | string | PAYWALL_EXIT_OFFER: the offering shown. |
| `package_id` | string | PAYWALL_PURCHASE_*: the package. |
| `product_id` | string | PAYWALL_PURCHASE_*: the product. |
| `error_code` | integer | PAYWALL_PURCHASE_ERROR. |
| `error_message` | string | PAYWALL_PURCHASE_ERROR. |
| `component_type` | string | PAYWALL_COMPONENT_INTERACTED: tab, package, purchase_button, sheet ... |
| `component_name` | string |  |
| `component_value` | string |  |
| `component_url` | string |  |
| `origin_index` | integer |  |
| `destination_index` | integer |  |
| `default_index` | integer |  |
| `origin_context_name` | string |  |
| `destination_context_name` | string |  |
| `origin_package_id` | string |  |
| `destination_package_id` | string |  |
| `default_package_id` | string |  |
| `origin_product_id` | string |  |
| `destination_product_id` | string |  |
| `default_product_id` | string |  |
| `current_package_id` | string |  |
| `resulting_package_id` | string |  |
| `current_product_id` | string |  |
| `resulting_product_id` | string |  |
| `sdk_version` | string | The customer's last SDK version. |
| `platform_version` | string | The customer's last OS version. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "id": "7D3F0B1E-5C2A-5E8B-9A4D-6F1E2C3B4A51",
    "type": "PAYWALL_IMPRESSION",
    "event_timestamp_ms": 1790800914034,
    "app_id": "app1a2b3c4d",
    "app_user_id": "user_42",
    "original_app_user_id": "$RCAnonymousID:9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a0",
    "aliases": [
      "$RCAnonymousID:9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a0",
      "user_42"
    ],
    "environment": "PRODUCTION",
    "store": "APP_STORE",
    "paywall_id": "pw_5k2m8q1x7c3z",
    "paywall_name": "Spring sale",
    "paywall_revision": 3,
    "offering_id": "default",
    "session_id": "0B6E2A4C-8D1F-4E3A-9C7B-5A2D8F1E6C3B",
    "display_mode": "full_screen",
    "dark_mode": false,
    "locale": "en_US",
    "placement_identifier": "onboarding",
    "sdk_version": "5.62.0",
    "platform_version": "18.5",
    "subscriber_attributes": {
      "$email": {
        "value": "wren@example.com",
        "updated_at_ms": 1790800000000
      }
    }
  }
```

## TEST

Sent by the dashboard's "Send test event" or `POST .../integrations/webhooks/{id}/test`. Shaped like a purchase, for no real customer, so it never carries `experiments`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Unique event id (upper-case UUID). Deduplicate on it. |
| `type` | string | Event type. |
| `event_timestamp_ms` | integer | When RevenueDot recorded the event. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `app_id` | string | RevenueDot app id. Left out for promotional grants. |
| `app_user_id` | string | The app user id the event is about (a non-anonymous alias when there is one). |
| `original_app_user_id` | string | The customer's first app user id. |
| `aliases` | array of string | Every app user id of the customer. |
| `product_id` | string | Store product id. For PRODUCT_CHANGE, the product the customer changed from. |
| `period_type` | `NORMAL`, `TRIAL`, `INTRO`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `PREPAID` |  |
| `purchased_at_ms` | integer | Start of the period. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `expiration_at_ms` | integer or null | End of the period, or null for lifetime. Epoch milliseconds. |
| `environment` | `PRODUCTION`, `SANDBOX` |  |
| `entitlement_id` | null | Always null (deprecated in RevenueCat's payload). |
| `entitlement_ids` | array of string | Lookup keys of the entitlements the product unlocks, or null. |
| `presented_offering_id` | string or null | Offering the purchase was made from, when the SDK sent it. |
| `transaction_id` | string or null | Store transaction id of this period. |
| `original_transaction_id` | string or null | First transaction id of the subscription. |
| `is_family_share` | boolean |  |
| `country_code` | string or null | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. |
| `currency` | string or null | ISO 4217. |
| `price` | number or null | USD. Money moved only on INITIAL_PURCHASE, RENEWAL, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE, REFUND_REVERSED and refunds (negative); 0 on other events. |
| `price_in_purchased_currency` | number or null | Same as price, in `currency`. |
| `subscriber_attributes` | object |  |
| `store` | `APP_STORE`, `MAC_APP_STORE`, `PLAY_STORE`, `AMAZON`, `STRIPE`, `RC_BILLING`, `PROMOTIONAL`, `TEST_STORE`, `PADDLE`, `ROKU`, `EXTERNAL` |  |
| `takehome_percentage` | number | 1 minus the estimated store commission. |
| `tax_percentage` | number | Always 0 today. |
| `commission_percentage` | number | Estimated store commission (0.3 for App Store and Google Play, 0 for Test Store). |
| `offer_code` | string or null | The App Store or Google Play offer id of this period (a promotional offer, offer code, win-back offer or Google offer), or null. See [Win-back offers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/win-back-offers.md). |
| `experiments` | array of object | Every offering experiment the customer joined. Left out when there are none. See [Experiments](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/guides/experiments.md#webhooks). |
| `experiments[].experiment_id` | string |  |
| `experiments[].experiment_variant` | `a`, `b`, `c`, `d` |  |
| `experiments[].enrolled_at_ms` | integer | Epoch milliseconds. |

Example:

```json
{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "event": {
    "id": "F48A3CEE-2785-4001-9A4D-590F95C1A9F0",
    "type": "TEST",
```

# What does Play Billing BILLING_UNAVAILABLE (3) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-billing-unavailable.md
Description: BILLING_UNAVAILABLE (3) means Google Play cannot bill this user: an old Play Store, an unsupported country, a blocked account or a declined payment method.

Play Billing BILLING_UNAVAILABLE (3) means a billing problem on the user's side stopped the purchase.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` (3) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | A user billing error occurred during processing. |

## Cause

- Google lists these examples: the Play Store app on the device is out of date, the user is in an unsupported country, an enterprise administrator has turned purchases off, or Google Play cannot charge the user's payment method (for example an expired card).
- Google also names a Play Store that the system blocks, for instance in an OEM kids mode, where the `BillingResult` debug message says the Play Store is blocked.
- These are conditions on the device or the account, so an automatic retry does not fix them.

## Fix

1. Do not retry automatically. A manual retry works only after the user fixes the condition, for example by updating the Play Store.
2. Show a short message and a **Try again** button; Google notes the user probably saw the reason in the Play purchase screen.
3. Read `debugMessage` and log it, because it can name the cause, such as a blocked Play Store.
4. Do not unlock content.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult

// No automatic retry: tell the person, and let them try again after they fix the account or update the Play Store.
fun onPurchaseResult(result: BillingResult, showMessage: (String) -> Unit) {
    if (result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.BILLING_UNAVAILABLE) {
        println("BILLING_UNAVAILABLE: ${result.debugMessage}")
        showMessage("Google Play cannot complete purchases right now. Check the Play Store and your payment method, then try again.")
    }
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` to `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseNotAllowedError` (code 3), the same code as `ITEM_NOT_OWNED` and `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED`. See [what purchaseNotAllowedError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-not-allowed-error.md).

# What does Play Billing DEVELOPER_ERROR (5) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-developer-error.md
Description: DEVELOPER_ERROR (5) means the app used the Play Billing API wrongly: bad arguments, an unsigned app or missing permissions. Read the debug message and fix the call.

Play Billing DEVELOPER_ERROR (5) means the app called the Play Billing API incorrectly.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.DEVELOPER_ERROR` (5) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The error comes from incorrect use of the API. |

## Cause

- Google's examples: invalid arguments such as an empty product list where one is required, or a misconfigured app, such as one that is not signed or lacks the permissions it needs in its manifest.
- Google also says that wrong parameters passed to `launchBillingFlow` can cause it, and that the debug message gives more detail.
- It is a fatal error for that call, so a retry with the same arguments fails again.

## Fix

1. Read `billingResult.debugMessage` and log it first; it usually names the problem.
2. Check the arguments of the failing call: a non-empty product list, product details from the same `BillingClient`, valid billing flow params.
3. Install a signed build: Google names an app that is not signed as one cause.
4. Check that the manifest has the permissions Google's integration guide requires, then rebuild.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult

// DEVELOPER_ERROR is a bug in how the app calls the API: the debug message is the fastest clue.
fun onBillingResult(result: BillingResult) {
    if (result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.DEVELOPER_ERROR) {
        println("DEVELOPER_ERROR: ${result.debugMessage}")
    }
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `DEVELOPER_ERROR` to `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseInvalidError` (code 4). See [what purchaseInvalidError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-invalid-error.md).

# What does Play Billing ERROR (6) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-error.md
Description: ERROR (6) means Google Play failed internally during a billing call. It can be transient: retry with exponential backoff, and contact Google Play if it persists.

Play Billing ERROR (6) means a fatal error inside Google Play during the billing call.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ERROR` (6) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | A fatal error occurred during the API action. |

## Cause

- Google describes it as an internal Google Play error that may be transient or caused by an unexpected condition during processing.
- The code does not say which call or condition failed, so the debug message and your own logs are the only detail.
- It is not caused by your arguments (that is `DEVELOPER_ERROR`) or by the network (that is `NETWORK_ERROR`).

## Fix

1. Retry with exponential backoff for background work; use a simple retry when the person is waiting.
2. Mind how long you retry during a user interaction, as Google advises.
3. Log the response code, debug message and Play Store version so you can report a persistent case.
4. Contact Google Play support if the error keeps coming back.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay

// Google: ERROR may be transient, so back off and retry a few times, then give up and report it.
suspend fun acknowledgeWithRetry(acknowledge: suspend () -> BillingResult): BillingResult {
    var wait = 2_000L
    var result = acknowledge()
    repeat(2) {
        if (result.responseCode != BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ERROR) return result
        delay(wait)
        wait *= 2
        result = acknowledge()
    }
    return result
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `ERROR` to `PurchasesErrorCode.StoreProblemError` (code 2). See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

# What does Play Billing FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED (-2) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-feature-not-supported.md
Description: FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED (-2) means the Play Store on the device does not support the Billing feature you called. It cannot be retried; check isFeatureSupported() first.

Play Billing FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED (-2) means the Google Play Billing feature you called is not supported on this device.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` (-2) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The requested feature is not supported by the Play Store on the current device. |

## Cause

- Google says the cause is likely an old Play Store version on the user's device. Its example is a device that does not support in-app messaging.
- Google lists it among the non-retriable responses: trying again on the same device gives the same answer.
- It is a property of the device and Play Store version, not of your app's configuration.

## Fix

1. Call `billingClient.isFeatureSupported(FeatureType)` before you use an optional feature, and only use the feature when the response is `OK`.
2. Do not retry the call. Hide the feature or use a fallback for that device.
3. Do not show a purchase error to the person: the product itself may still be sellable without the optional feature.
4. Keep the Billing Library current, because newer versions know more feature types.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient

// Ask before you use an optional feature. FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED cannot be fixed by retrying.
fun supportsInAppMessaging(billingClient: BillingClient): Boolean {
    if (!billingClient.isReady) return false
    val result = billingClient.isFeatureSupported(BillingClient.FeatureType.IN_APP_MESSAGING)
    return result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.OK
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` to `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseNotAllowedError` (code 3), the same code it uses for `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE` and `ITEM_NOT_OWNED`. See [what purchaseNotAllowedError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-not-allowed-error.md).

# What does Play Billing ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED (7) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-item-already-owned.md
Description: ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED (7) means the user already owns the product. Query purchases, grant what they own and do not offer the product again.

Play Billing ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED (7) means the user already owns the subscription or one-time product they tried to buy.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED` (7) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The purchase failed because the item is already owned. |

## Cause

- Google says the Google Play user already owns the product. In most cases this is not transient, except when stale purchase data cached by Play causes it.
- A stale cache is refreshed when you receive the error, so a retry after the refresh can succeed.
- Your app offered a product the user owns because it did not check what the user already has.

## Fix

1. Call `queryPurchasesAsync()` after the error to see what the user owns, and process those purchases (grant access, acknowledge or consume).
2. If the user does not own the product after that, retry the purchase once; the cache has been updated.
3. Prevent it: check the user's entitlements when you list products, and do not offer products the user already owns.
4. Tell the person "You already have this" instead of showing a failure.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult
import com.android.billingclient.api.QueryPurchasesParams

// Treat ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED as good news: fetch what the user owns and grant it (Google's recommended fix).
fun onPurchaseResult(client: BillingClient, result: BillingResult) {
    if (result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED) {
        val params = QueryPurchasesParams.newBuilder().setProductType(BillingClient.ProductType.SUBS).build()
        client.queryPurchasesAsync(params) { queryResult, purchases ->
            if (queryResult.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.OK) {
                purchases.forEach { println("Already owned: ${it.products}") }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED` to `PurchasesErrorCode.ProductAlreadyPurchasedError` (code 6). Call `restorePurchases()` or `getCustomerInfo()` to give the customer the entitlement they already paid for. See [what productAlreadyPurchasedError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-product-already-purchased-error.md).

# What does Play Billing ITEM_NOT_OWNED (8) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-item-not-owned.md
Description: ITEM_NOT_OWNED (8) means the user does not own the product you tried to replace, acknowledge or consume. Query purchases first and reconcile.

Play Billing ITEM_NOT_OWNED (8) means the action failed because the user does not own the item it targeted.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ITEM_NOT_OWNED` (8) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The requested action on the item failed because the user does not own it. |

## Cause

- Google says the user does not own the subscription or one-time product they tried to replace, acknowledge or consume. It is not transient in most cases, except when Google Play's cache is stale.
- A stale cache is refreshed when the error is received, so the data is correct on the next call.
- Google's own example: you try to consume an item and the updated purchase data says it is already consumed, so the error can be ignored.

## Fix

1. Call `queryPurchasesAsync()` after the error to get the current purchases.
2. If the updated purchase list shows the item is already consumed, ignore the error. If the user owns it, redo the action.
3. If the user does not own it at all, stop the action; do not grant access.
4. Make acknowledge and consume calls idempotent, keyed by the purchase token.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult
import com.android.billingclient.api.QueryPurchasesParams

// After ITEM_NOT_OWNED, trust the fresh purchase list, not the purchase you held: it may already be consumed.
fun onAcknowledgeResult(client: BillingClient, result: BillingResult) {
    if (result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ITEM_NOT_OWNED) {
        val params = QueryPurchasesParams.newBuilder().setProductType(BillingClient.ProductType.INAPP).build()
        client.queryPurchasesAsync(params) { _, purchases ->
            println("The user currently owns ${purchases.size} one-time products")
        }
    }
}
```

# What does Play Billing ITEM_UNAVAILABLE (4) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-item-unavailable.md
Description: ITEM_UNAVAILABLE (4) means the product cannot be bought by this user. Check that it is active, the app is published and the product is sold in the user's country.

Play Billing ITEM_UNAVAILABLE (4) means the product you asked to buy is not available for purchase for this user.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ITEM_UNAVAILABLE` (4) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The requested product is not available for purchase. |

## Cause

- Google says a product must be active, its app must be published and its app must be available in the user's country to be sold.
- A product that is configured for another region than the user's returns this code. Google also says a change of country availability can take time to spread, so the code can appear after a correct change.
- During testing, a correct configuration can still return it for a while because product details take time to propagate across Google's servers.

## Fix

1. Refresh product details with `queryProductDetailsAsync` and only sell products that it returns.
2. Check the product's state, the app's publishing state and the product's country availability in Play Console.
3. If you changed availability recently, wait and try again later.
4. Hide the buy button for a product that did not come back from `queryProductDetailsAsync`.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult

// ITEM_UNAVAILABLE is a catalog problem: log the product ID and hide the button instead of retrying.
fun onPurchaseResult(result: BillingResult, productId: String, hideProduct: (String) -> Unit) {
    if (result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.ITEM_UNAVAILABLE) {
        println("ITEM_UNAVAILABLE for $productId: check it is active, the app is published and the country is allowed")
        hideProduct(productId)
    }
}
```

# What does Play Billing NETWORK_ERROR (12) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-network-error.md
Description: NETWORK_ERROR (12) means the device could not reach Google Play. Retry once the connection returns, with backoff for background calls. Billing Library 6 and later.

Play Billing NETWORK_ERROR (12) means a network problem stopped the device from reaching Google Play.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.NETWORK_ERROR` (12) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | A network error occurred during the operation. |

## Cause

- Google says there was a problem with the network connection between the device and Play systems, which can also mean the user has no active connection.
- The code is returned only by Billing Library 6 and later. Earlier versions returned `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` for network problems.
- It comes from the connection, not from your product setup or your API arguments.

## Fix

1. Retry with a simple retry when the person is waiting, or exponential backoff for background calls such as acknowledging a purchase.
2. Show "Check your connection and try again" and keep the screen usable with cached data.
3. Do not unlock content from this error; unlock from a purchase the Play Store reports as purchased.
4. Update to Billing Library 6 or later if you still see `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` for network problems.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult

// A dropped connection is retryable: ask the person to try again instead of showing a failure.
fun onBillingResult(result: BillingResult, showMessage: (String) -> Unit) {
    if (result.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.NETWORK_ERROR) {
        showMessage("Check your connection and try again.")
    }
}
```

# What does Play Billing SERVICE_DISCONNECTED (-1) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-service-disconnected.md
Description: SERVICE_DISCONNECTED (-1) means the app lost its connection to the Play Store service. Enable automatic reconnection, check isReady and retry with backoff.

Play Billing SERVICE_DISCONNECTED (-1) means the app is not connected to the Google Play Store service through the Billing Library.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.SERVICE_DISCONNECTED` (-1) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The app is not connected to the Play Store service through the Google Play Billing Library. |

## Cause

- Google lists two examples: the Play Store was updated in the background while the app ran and the library lost the connection, or `startConnection()` was never called or has not finished yet.
- Google calls the state transient, so the right answer is a reconnect and a retry, not a message that a purchase failed.
- Billing Library 8.0.0 added `enableAutoServiceReconnection()`, which reconnects when you make a call while disconnected.

## Fix

1. Enable automatic service reconnection when you build the `BillingClient`. Google strongly recommends it from version 8.0.0.
2. If you do not use it, check `billingClient.isReady` before every call and call `startConnection()` again after a disconnect.
3. If you still get the code after automatic reconnection, retry: simply for actions the person is waiting on, and with exponential backoff for background work.
4. Cap the number of retries: Google's own example stops after three attempts, two seconds apart.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.PendingPurchasesParams
import com.android.billingclient.api.PurchasesUpdatedListener

// Let the library reconnect for you; this is Google's recommended fix for SERVICE_DISCONNECTED (Billing Library 8.0.0 or later).
fun buildClient(context: android.content.Context, listener: PurchasesUpdatedListener): BillingClient =
    BillingClient.newBuilder(context)
        .setListener(listener)
        .enablePendingPurchases(PendingPurchasesParams.newBuilder().enableOneTimeProducts().build())
        .enableAutoServiceReconnection()
        .build()
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED` to `PurchasesErrorCode.StoreProblemError` (code 2). The SDK owns the `BillingClient` and reconnects on its own, so your app sees the error only when that fails. See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

# What does Play Billing SERVICE_TIMEOUT (-3) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-service-timeout.md
Description: SERVICE_TIMEOUT (-3) means Google Play did not answer before the request timed out. Only Billing Library 5.2.0 and earlier return it; retry the same call, with backoff in the background.

Play Billing SERVICE_TIMEOUT (-3) means a request reached its maximum timeout before Google Play could answer.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.SERVICE_TIMEOUT` (-3) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The request has reached the maximum timeout before Google Play responds. |

## Cause

- Google gives an example: a delay in executing the action that the Billing Library call asked for.
- Only Billing Library 5.2.0 and earlier return it. From 6.0.0 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` is returned for the same problem and `SERVICE_TIMEOUT` is deprecated.
- Unlike `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED`, the connection to the billing service is still up.

## Fix

1. Retry the same Billing Library call. Use a simple retry for something the person waits on, and exponential backoff for background work.
2. Do not call `startConnection()` again, because the connection is not severed.
3. Upgrade the Billing Library. Version 8 is required for new apps and updates from 2026-08-31, and it never returns this code.
4. Treat `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` the same way, so one handler covers both.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay

// Retry the same call on a timeout; the connection is fine (Google's guidance for code -3).
suspend fun <T> retryOnTimeout(maxTries: Int = 3, call: suspend () -> Pair<BillingResult, T>): Pair<BillingResult, T> {
    var result = call()
    var tries = 1
    while (result.first.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.SERVICE_TIMEOUT && tries < maxTries) {
        delay(2_000L * tries)
        result = call()
        tries++
    }
    return result
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `SERVICE_TIMEOUT` to `PurchasesErrorCode.StoreProblemError` (code 2) and, inside its own billing code, treats it as `ServiceUnavailable`. See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

# What does Play Billing SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (2) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-service-unavailable.md
Description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (2) means the Google Play billing service is unavailable right now. It is transient: retry the same call, with backoff in the background.

Play Billing SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (2) means the Google Play billing service is temporarily unavailable.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (2) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The service is currently unavailable. |

## Cause

- Google says the billing service is currently unavailable; in most cases a network problem between the device and Google Play billing is behind it.
- From Billing Library 6.0.0 the code is no longer returned for network issues. Those now return `NETWORK_ERROR`, and `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` also replaces the deprecated `SERVICE_TIMEOUT`.
- Unlike `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED`, the connection is still up, so only the operation needs a retry.

## Fix

1. Retry the same call. For something the person is waiting on, use a simple retry with a maximum number of attempts.
2. For background work such as acknowledging a purchase, retry with exponential backoff.
3. Do not call `startConnection()` again; the connection is not severed.
4. Keep the number of retries small while the person waits, and then show a message with a Try again button.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay

// Retry the same call: the connection is fine, the service was briefly unavailable (Google's guidance for code 2).
suspend fun <T> retryOnUnavailable(maxTries: Int = 3, call: suspend () -> Pair<BillingResult, T>): Pair<BillingResult, T> {
    var delayMs = 2_000L
    var result = call()
    var tries = 1
    while (result.first.responseCode == BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE && tries < maxTries) {
        delay(delayMs)
        delayMs *= 2 // exponential backoff, for work the person is not waiting on
        result = call()
        tries++
    }
    return result
}
```

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` to `PurchasesErrorCode.StoreProblemError` (code 2). Retrying once is reasonable. See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

# What does Play Billing USER_CANCELED (1) mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-user-canceled.md
Description: USER_CANCELED (1) means the user left the Play billing screen without buying. It is not an error: show nothing and keep the paywall open.

Play Billing USER_CANCELED (1) means the user closed the billing flow before finishing the purchase.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.USER_CANCELED` (1) |
| Where | Google Play Billing Library (`BillingResult.responseCode`) |
| What the vendor says | The transaction was canceled by the user. |

## Cause

- Google lists it as a response that does not indicate an error: for actions that show a Play Store screen, it means the user left that screen without finishing.
- Nothing was bought and nothing is broken; the person made a choice.
- Google calls it informational and says the app can fail gracefully.

## Fix

1. Do not show an error dialog.
2. Leave the paywall open with its products loaded so the person can choose again.
3. Count cancels apart from failures in analytics.
4. Do not retry for the person and do not unlock anything.

## Example

```kotlin
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingClient
import com.android.billingclient.api.BillingResult

// A cancel is the person's choice: no dialog, no retry. Log it at info level so real failures stay visible.
fun onPurchasesUpdated(result: BillingResult) {
    when (result.responseCode) {
        BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.USER_CANCELED -> println("Purchase cancelled by the user")
        BillingClient.BillingResponseCode.OK -> println("Purchase flow finished")
        else -> println("Billing result ${result.responseCode}: ${result.debugMessage}")
    }
}
```

*Not compiled: this Kotlin snippet was not built here because the docs repo has no Kotlin or Android toolchain. Check it against your Play Billing Library or SDK version before you ship it.*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-android` fork maps `USER_CANCELED` to `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseCancelledError` (code 1) and sets the `userCancelled` flag in the purchase callback. See [what purchaseCancelledError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-cancelled-error.md).

# What does configurationError (code 23) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-configuration-error.md
Description: configurationError (code 23) means your setup does not line up: no offering product could be fetched from the store, or the backend said the platform is invalid (7000).

The purchases SDK raises configurationError (code 23) when its setup does not match the store or the server.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.configurationError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.ConfigurationError` (Android), code 23 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | There is an issue with your configuration. Check the underlying error for more details. |

## Cause

- iOS: none of the products in your offerings could be fetched from App Store Connect, or from the StoreKit configuration file when one is in use.
- An offering exists but has no products for this app's store, or the API key belongs to a store with no products registered.
- The backend answered 7000 (invalid platform), 7255 (could not create alias) or 8077; Android also maps 7230 (invalid package name) here.

## Fix

1. Compare product IDs: the ID in the offering must equal the store's product ID exactly, and each product must be approved and ready to sell.
2. Use the iOS app's key in the iOS build and the Android app's key in the Android build.
3. Mark an offering as current and add this app's products to its packages.
4. Read the SDK's message with debug logs; it says which case applies.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .configurationError:
        // A setup problem: do not retry. Alert yourself and show a neutral message.
        print("The SDK configuration does not match the store")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

# What does invalidCredentialsError (code 11) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-invalid-credentials-error.md
Description: invalidCredentialsError (code 11) means the backend rejected the SDK's API key or an auth token, usually code 7225. Copy the app's public SDK key again.

The purchases SDK raises invalidCredentialsError (code 11) when the backend rejects the API key or an auth token.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.invalidCredentialsError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.InvalidCredentialsError` (Android), code 11 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | There was a credentials issue. Check the underlying error for more details. |

## Cause

- The backend answered 7225 (invalid API key) or 7224 (invalid auth token). iOS also maps 7104 (invalid App Store shared secret) and 7981, and Android maps 7107 (invalid Play Store credentials).
- The key has a typo, or it belongs to another project or another server; a RevenueCat key sent to RevenueDot is unknown, and the reverse.
- The proxy URL was set after `configure`, or the key is of the wrong kind, such as a `test_` Test Store key in a release build.

## Fix

1. Copy the app's public SDK key again from the app page and check each character.
2. Set `Purchases.proxyURL` before `Purchases.configure`.
3. Use the iOS app's key in the iOS build and the Android app's key in the Android build.
4. On iOS, `PurchasesDiagnostics.default.testSDKHealth()` reports an invalid API key as such.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .invalidCredentialsError:
        // The key stays wrong until you fix it: alert yourself, show customers a generic message.
        print("The API key was rejected")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

RevenueDot answers 401 with code 7225 for an unknown key. See [the server error codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/errors.md). Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/invalid-credentials-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/invalid-credentials-error).

# What does invalidReceiptError (code 8) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-invalid-receipt-error.md
Description: invalidReceiptError (code 8) means the backend said the receipt or purchase token is not valid, usually code 7103. Check the bundle ID or package name and the store credentials.

The purchases SDK raises invalidReceiptError (code 8) when the backend rejects the receipt, signed transaction or purchase token.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.invalidReceiptError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.InvalidReceiptError` (Android), code 8 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | The receipt is not valid. |

## Cause

- The backend answered 7103 (invalid receipt token) or, on iOS, 7712 (the purchased product is missing from the Apple receipt).
- The receipt came from a build with a different bundle ID or package name than the app configured on the server.
- A StoreKit testing receipt signed by Xcode's local certificate reached a server that does not know that certificate, or Google Play says the purchase token is invalid.

## Fix

1. Compare the app's `bundle_id` or `package_name` on the server with the build you test.
2. For StoreKit testing in Xcode, add the public certificate from your `.storekit` file as the app's `xcode_certificate` credential.
3. Read the server message in the underlying error; the 7103 message names the cause.
4. Run the credential check on the app page: a wrong App Store key or Google service account is a server setup problem, not a bad receipt.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .invalidReceiptError:
        // A 4xx answer means the receipt can never be accepted: do not retry, point the customer to support.
        print("The receipt could not be verified")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

RevenueDot's server answers 400 with code 7103, and the SDK then finishes the transaction for good. See [4xx or 5xx on a receipt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/receipt-errors-4xx-vs-5xx.md). Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/invalid-receipt-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/invalid-receipt-error).
