# What does networkError (code 10) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-network-error.md
Description: networkError (code 10) means a request could not finish on the network: a timeout, a dropped connection or an unreachable host. It is temporary, so retry after a pause.

The purchases SDK raises networkError (code 10) when a request fails at the network layer.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.networkError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.NetworkError` (Android), code 10 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | A network error has occurred. |

## Cause

- iOS: any `URLSession` failure other than "not connected to the Internet" (which becomes `offlineConnectionError`) maps here.
- Android: an `IOException` or `JSONException` while performing the request, and Play Billing `NETWORK_ERROR`.
- A wrong proxy URL: a typo, `http` instead of `https`, a missing port, or `localhost` on an Android emulator, where `localhost` is the emulator itself.

## Fix

1. Retry after a short wait and back off if it fails again.
2. Set the proxy URL before `configure`. On an Android emulator use `http://10.0.2.2:8787` for a server on your computer, or HTTPS.
3. On iOS, call `PurchasesDiagnostics.default.testSDKHealth()` to see whether the SDK can reach the server.
4. Read the underlying error: on iOS `NSUnderlyingErrorKey` holds the `URLError` with the real reason.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .networkError:
        // Retrying is safe: the SDK keeps unposted purchases and sends them again later.
        print("Network problem; try again soon")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

If RevenueDot is unreachable the SDK sees a connection error; if it answers 5xx the SDK keeps the transaction and retries. Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/network-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/network-error).

- [What does offlineConnectionError (code 35) mean in the purchases SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-offline-connection-error.md)

# What does offlineConnectionError (code 35) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-offline-connection-error.md
Description: offlineConnectionError (code 35) means the device is offline. Show an offline message, retry when the connection returns and rely on cached customer info.

The purchases SDK raises offlineConnectionError (code 35) on iOS when a request fails because the device is not connected to the internet.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.offlineConnectionError` (iOS), no Android member, code 35 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | Error performing request because the internet connection appears to be offline. |

## Cause

- A request failed with the system's "not connected to the Internet" error, which the SDK maps to this error. It differs from `networkError`, which covers every other network failure.
- Airplane mode, no signal, Wi-Fi without internet, or cellular data blocked for the app.
- Android has no member for this code; the same situation raises an `IOException`, which becomes `NetworkError`.

## Fix

1. Show an offline state and keep the app usable with cached data.
2. Retry offerings or customer info when your platform's reachability callback says the network is back.
3. Keep gating features on the cached entitlement state the SDK already holds.
4. On iOS, check that cellular data is allowed for the app in Settings.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .offlineConnectionError:
        // Offline is not a purchase failure: keep cached access and retry when the network returns.
        print("You appear to be offline")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

Customers who already paid keep the access the SDK cached, and a device that is offline never reaches RevenueDot. Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/offline-connection-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/offline-connection-error).

# What does paymentPendingError (code 20) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-payment-pending-error.md
Description: paymentPendingError (code 20) means the purchase started but is not paid yet: Ask to Buy approval, a bank check or a delayed Google Play payment. It is not a failure.

The purchases SDK raises paymentPendingError (code 20) when a purchase is pending and not yet paid.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.paymentPendingError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.PaymentPendingError` (Android), code 20 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | The payment is pending. |

## Cause

- StoreKit 2: the purchase result is `.pending`, which Apple describes as a purchase that requires action from the customer.
- StoreKit 1: a transaction in the `deferred` state, for example Ask to Buy.
- Android: the Play purchase state is `PENDING`. Google says to grant the entitlement only when the state is `PURCHASED`.

## Fix

1. Show a pending message such as "Your purchase is waiting for approval" and close the paywall.
2. Listen for updates: `PurchasesDelegate` on iOS, `UpdatedCustomerInfoListener` on Android.
3. Call `getCustomerInfo` when the app comes back to the foreground; a pending purchase can complete while the app is closed.
4. On Android, acknowledge only after the state is `PURCHASED`.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .paymentPendingError:
        // Not a failure: show a pending message and wait for the customer info update.
        print("Payment pending; do not unlock yet")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

Do not retry the purchase, or the customer starts a second one. Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/payment-pending-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/payment-pending-error).

# What does productAlreadyPurchasedError (code 6) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-product-already-purchased-error.md
Description: productAlreadyPurchasedError (code 6) means the customer already owns the product. Refresh customer info or restore purchases instead of selling it again.

The purchases SDK raises productAlreadyPurchasedError (code 6) when the store refuses to sell a product the customer already owns.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.productAlreadyPurchasedError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.ProductAlreadyPurchasedError` (Android), code 6 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | This product is already active for the user. |

## Cause

- Android: Play Billing `ITEM_ALREADY_OWNED`. Google says it is usually permanent but can be stale cache, and recommends `queryPurchasesAsync()`.
- StoreKit 1: an `unknown` `SKError` whose underlying error says the customer is currently subscribed.
- On Android, the backend answered 7852 (a web purchase that belongs to another user); iOS reports that as `purchaseBelongsToOtherUser` instead.

## Fix

1. Call `getCustomerInfo` and check the entitlement. If it is active, close the paywall.
2. If it is not active, call `restorePurchases()` so the SDK posts the owned purchase.
3. On Android, acknowledge or consume purchases so they do not stay owned and block a second purchase.
4. Hide the buy button for owners by checking the entitlement before you show the paywall.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .productAlreadyPurchasedError:
        // Good news: the customer already owns it. Refresh customer info or restore, then close the paywall.
        print("Already purchased; restore or refresh customer info")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

# What does productNotAvailableForPurchaseError (code 5) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-product-not-available-for-purchase-error.md
Description: productNotAvailableForPurchaseError (code 5) means the store has no purchasable product for this customer. Check the product ID, its state and its regions.

The purchases SDK raises productNotAvailableForPurchaseError (code 5) when the store reports the product as unavailable for this customer.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.productNotAvailableForPurchaseError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.ProductNotAvailableForPurchaseError` (Android), code 5 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | The product is not available for purchase. |

## Cause

- StoreKit 1: `SKError.storeProductNotAvailable`. StoreKit 2: `StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront` and `Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable`.
- Android: Play Billing `ITEM_UNAVAILABLE`. Google says to refresh product details and check the product's configuration and country availability.
- In the RevenueDot Android SDK's Test Store, a product with no price also raises this error.

## Fix

1. Check the product in App Store Connect or Play Console: it must exist, be approved or active and be sold in the customer's country.
2. Match the product ID exactly. The ID in your offering must equal the store's product ID.
3. Wait after you create a product, then test again with a fresh install.
4. Hide the package so the customer is not stuck on a button that cannot work.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .productNotAvailableForPurchaseError:
        // Do not retry the same call: hide the package and log the product ID.
        print("The product is not available for purchase")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

In RevenueDot, a product whose `store_identifier` differs from the store's ID returns no product from the store. # What does purchaseCancelledError (code 1) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-cancelled-error.md
Description: purchaseCancelledError (code 1) means the customer closed the purchase sheet. Nothing was bought and nothing is broken: show no error and keep the paywall open.

The purchases SDK raises purchaseCancelledError (code 1) when the customer closes the purchase sheet without buying.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.purchaseCancelledError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseCancelledError` (Android), code 1 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | Purchase was cancelled. |

## Cause

- StoreKit 2 reports `StoreKitError.userCancelled` and StoreKit 1 reports `SKError.paymentCancelled`; the SDK maps both to this error.
- On Android, Play Billing returns `USER_CANCELED` when the customer leaves the billing flow, and the SDK maps it here ([Google docs](https://developer.android.com/google/play/billing/errors)).
- The Cancel button in the Test Store purchase dialog raises it too, so a tester can see it without leaving the app.

## Fix

1. Treat it as an outcome, not an error. In the Swift async API read `userCancelled` on the result; in callbacks read the `userCancelled` flag.
2. Leave the paywall open with its products loaded so the customer can choose again.
3. Count cancels apart from failures in analytics.
4. Turn on debug logs if a tester says they did not cancel; the underlying error shows who reported the cancel.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .purchaseCancelledError:
        // A cancel is the customer's choice: no dialog, no retry, nothing to unlock.
        print("Purchase cancelled")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

RevenueDot never sees a cancelled purchase, because the SDK stops before it posts a receipt to `POST /v1/receipts`. Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/purchase-cancelled-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/purchase-cancelled-error).

# What does purchaseInvalidError (code 4) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-invalid-error.md
Description: purchaseInvalidError (code 4) means one or more arguments of the purchase are not valid. Check the product, offer and options you pass, and read the underlying error.

The purchases SDK raises purchaseInvalidError (code 4) when the store or the backend says an argument of the purchase is not valid.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.purchaseInvalidError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseInvalidError` (Android), code 4 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | One or more of the arguments provided are invalid. |

## Cause

- Android: Play Billing `DEVELOPER_ERROR`, the code Google uses for incorrect use of the API, maps here.
- StoreKit 2: `StoreKitError.unsupported` maps here when the SDK is built with Swift 6.1 or later.
- The backend answered a code the SDK treats as an invalid purchase request, such as 7105 (invalid payment mode) or 7106 (missing Google product ID), or an invalid web redemption token.

## Fix

1. Read the underlying error and the debug message; they name the invalid argument.
2. Check the product, offer and options you pass against what is configured in the store and on the server.
3. On Android, check for a signed build and a non-empty product list, as Google lists for `DEVELOPER_ERROR`.
4. Do not retry with the same arguments; the result will not change.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .purchaseInvalidError:
        // A bug in the arguments: log the underlying error and fix the call, do not retry.
        print("The purchase arguments are invalid")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

# What does purchaseNotAllowedError (code 3) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-not-allowed-error.md
Description: purchaseNotAllowedError (code 3) means this device or account may not buy: purchases are restricted, or Google Play billing is unavailable. Retrying does not help.

The purchases SDK raises purchaseNotAllowedError (code 3) when the device or account is not allowed to make the purchase.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.purchaseNotAllowedError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.PurchaseNotAllowedError` (Android), code 3 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | The device or user is not allowed to make the purchase. |

## Cause

- StoreKit 2: `Product.PurchaseError.purchaseNotAllowed`, which Apple documents as the user not being allowed to make purchases. StoreKit 1: `SKError.paymentNotAllowed` and several related codes.
- Android: Play Billing `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE`, `ITEM_NOT_OWNED` and `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` map here. Google lists an outdated Play Store, an unsupported country and a declined payment method as reasons for `BILLING_UNAVAILABLE`.
- A product change (upgrade or downgrade) requested for a product that is not a subscription.

## Fix

1. Check before you show the paywall: `Purchases.canMakePayments()` on iOS, or the Android equivalent with a callback.
2. Ask the customer to check restrictions: Screen Time or a device management profile on iOS, an up-to-date Play Store, a supported country and a valid payment method on Android.
3. Test on a real store account. Simulators and emulators without one return this error.
4. Do not retry. The block stays until the customer changes a setting.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .purchaseNotAllowedError:
        // Retrying cannot help: explain the block and show the paywall again on the next launch.
        print("Purchases are not allowed on this device or account")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

# What does receiptAlreadyInUseError (code 7) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-receipt-already-in-use-error.md
Description: receiptAlreadyInUseError (code 7) means the purchase belongs to another app user and the project's transfer setting forbids moving it. Backend code 7102.

The purchases SDK raises receiptAlreadyInUseError (code 7) when the backend refuses to move a purchase that already belongs to another app user.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.receiptAlreadyInUseError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.ReceiptAlreadyInUseError` (Android), code 7 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | There is already another active subscriber using the same receipt. |

## Cause

- The backend answered 7102 (cannot transfer purchase), and both SDKs map it to this error.
- A customer restored or re-posted a store purchase while signed in as a different app user than the one who bought it.
- The project's restore behavior forbids moving the purchase. A shared device, or a new app user ID after logging out, leaves the old account as the owner.

## Fix

1. Find the current owner: open the customer in the dashboard or call `GET /v1/subscribers/{app_user_id}` for the suspected owner.
2. Ask the customer to sign in with the account that bought; entitlements appear without a restore.
3. Pick the right `transfer_behavior`: `transfer`, `transfer_if_no_active`, `keep` or `share`.
4. Use one app user ID per person with `logIn`, so purchases stay on one customer across devices.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .receiptAlreadyInUseError:
        // Same request, same answer: tell the customer which account bought, never whose account it is.
        print("This purchase is linked to another account")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

RevenueDot answers HTTP 400 with code 7102 when the project's `transfer_behavior` is `keep`, or `transfer_if_no_active` and the owner is still active. See [how to restore purchases](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/restore-purchases.md) and [the server error codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/errors.md). Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/receipt-already-in-use-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/receipt-already-in-use-error).

# What does signatureVerificationFailed (code 37) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-signature-verification-failed.md
Description: signatureVerificationFailed (code 37 on iOS, 36 on Android) means a response failed the SDK's signature check. It is thrown only when verification is enforced.

The purchases SDK raises signatureVerificationFailed (code 37 on iOS, 36 on Android) when a response fails the signature check and verification is enforced.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.signatureVerificationFailed` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.SignatureVerificationError` (Android), code 37 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | Request failed signature verification. |

## Cause

- iOS: a response failed verification while the SDK was in enforced mode. In any other mode the SDK logs the failure and carries on.
- Android: a `SignatureVerificationException` becomes `SignatureVerificationError`, numbered 36 on Android and 37 on iOS.
- A server that does not sign with the key the SDK trusts. The stock SDK trusts only RevenueCat's key, and a proxy that rewrites responses breaks the signature too.

## Fix

1. Turn verification off in the SDK configuration (disabled mode). Native iOS and Android default to informational mode, which only logs a failure.
2. Never use enforced mode with the stock SDK against RevenueDot: it would reject every response.
3. Or build the RevenueDot forks with your server's public signing key to get verified responses.
4. Compare the key at `GET /.well-known/revenuedot-signing-key` with the key in your SDK build.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .signatureVerificationFailed:
        // In informational mode nothing is thrown; with enforcement on, never unlock from this response.
        print("Signature verification failed")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

RevenueDot signs 2xx and 3xx responses under `/v1` when `REVENUEDOT_SIGNING_KEY` is set. See [signature verification failed in proxy mode](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/help/signature-verification-failed.md). Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/signature-verification-failed](https://revenuedot.app/errors/signature-verification-failed).

# What does storeProblemError (code 2) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md
Description: storeProblemError (code 2) means the App Store, Google Play or the payment system failed the request. It is usually temporary: retry once and read the underlying error.

The purchases SDK raises storeProblemError (code 2) when the App Store or Google Play fails a request or the backend reports a store problem.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.StoreProblemError` (Android), code 2 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | There was a problem with the store. |

## Cause

- StoreKit 2: `StoreKitError.systemError`, `.notEntitled` and `.unknown`, and `Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity` all map here.
- Android: Play Billing `ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED` and `SERVICE_TIMEOUT` map here. Google describes `ERROR` as an internal Play problem and `SERVICE_DISCONNECTED` as a severed connection ([Google docs](https://developer.android.com/google/play/billing/errors)).
- The backend answered 7101 (store problem), or on Android 7229 (Play quota exceeded) or 7231 (Play generic error).

## Fix

1. Read the underlying error: `NSUnderlyingErrorKey` and `rc_backend_error_code` on iOS, `underlyingErrorMessage` on Android. They tell a StoreKit failure from a backend 7101.
2. Retry once after a short pause. Google recommends retries with backoff for `ERROR` and service disconnects.
3. Check that the store account on the device works: open the App Store or Google Play once and try again.
4. If the backend sent 7101, fix the store key or service account the message names, using Verify credentials on the app page.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .storeProblemError:
        // Retrying once is reasonable; never unlock until customer info shows the entitlement.
        print("The store had a problem; read the underlying error")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

A burst of storeProblemError usually means a store outage or a broken store credential on the server. See the [server error codes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/api/errors.md) for 7101. Deep dive: [revenuedot.app/errors/store-problem-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/store-problem-error).

# What does unknownError (code 0) mean in the purchases SDK?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-unknown-error.md
Description: unknownError (code 0) is the purchases SDK's catch-all for a failure it cannot classify. Read the underlying error, turn on debug logs and update the SDK.

The purchases SDK raises unknownError (code 0) when a failure matches none of its named errors.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `ErrorCode.unknownError` (iOS), `PurchasesErrorCode.UnknownError` (Android), code 0 |
| Where | Purchases SDK (iOS, Android and the hybrid SDKs built on them) |
| What the vendor says | Unknown error. Check the underlying error for more details. |

## Cause

- A StoreKit or Play Billing error that the SDK has no mapping for. On iOS, `StoreKitError` cases that are newer than the SDK fall through to this error, and so does any other unmapped error.
- On Android, an exception that is not a network, security or signature failure becomes `UnknownError`, and so does any Play Billing response code outside the known list ([errors.kt](https://github.com/revenuedot/purchases-android/blob/revenuedot/main-patches/purchases/src/main/kotlin/com/revenuecat/purchases/google/errors.kt)).
- The backend answered with code 0, which the SDK reads as "we do not know what happened".

## Fix

1. Read the underlying error: on iOS `NSUnderlyingErrorKey` and `readable_error_code` in `userInfo`, on Android `error.underlyingErrorMessage`.
2. Turn on debug logs (`Purchases.logLevel = .debug`) and read the lines before the error.
3. Update the SDK. A StoreKit or Play error that is new to the operating system can be unmapped in an old release.
4. Do not unlock content and do not retry automatically; let the customer try again.

## Example

```swift
// The purchases SDK throws `ErrorCode` values; match the one you handle and let the rest fall through.
func handle(_ error: Error) {
    guard let code = error as? ErrorCode else {
        print("Not a purchases SDK error: \(error)")
        return
    }
    switch code {
    case .unknownError:
        print("Unknown failure: read the underlying error and the debug log")
    default:
        print("Other purchases error: \(code.description)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` together with the `ErrorCode.swift` file of the RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

RevenueDot answers server failures with a numeric `code`, so a server problem reaches the SDK as a backend error and not as `unknownError`. The full deep dive is on [revenuedot.app/errors/unknown-error](https://revenuedot.app/errors/unknown-error).

# What does StoreKitError.invalidPresentationContext mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-invalid-presentation-context.md
Description: StoreKitError.invalidPresentationContext means StoreKit cannot show its UI from the current context. Call StoreKit views and sheets from a visible scene on the main actor. Available from iOS 27.

StoreKitError.invalidPresentationContext means StoreKit tried to show its own screen and could not, because the context it was given cannot present one.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.invalidPresentationContext` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 27.0, iPadOS 27.0, macOS 27.0, tvOS 27.0, watchOS 27.0, visionOS 27.0 |
| What the vendor says | StoreKit UI cannot be presented from the current context. |

## Cause

- Apple's case page gives only that one line. The case is listed under the enumeration cases of `StoreKitError`, separate from the other error codes.
- StoreKit shows system UI for purchase confirmation, refund requests and offer redemption. Each needs a window or scene to present from.
- The availability line in the StoreKit interface of the Xcode 27 SDK marks the case as new in version 27, so earlier systems never throw it.

## Fix

1. Start the StoreKit call from the main actor and while the app has a foreground scene, for example from a button handler.
2. Pass the scene that is on screen when an API takes one (`beginRefundRequest(in:)` takes a `UIWindowScene`).
3. Do not start purchase or refund flows from a background task, an extension or a scene that is closing.
4. Retry after the scene is visible again, and show a short message if it still fails.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// invalidPresentationContext is new in version 27 systems, so check availability before you name it.
func describe(_ error: Error) -> String {
    if #available(iOS 27.0, macOS 27.0, tvOS 27.0, watchOS 27.0, visionOS 27.0, *),
       case StoreKitError.invalidPresentationContext = error {
        return "StoreKit could not show its screen from here; try again from a visible scene"
    }
    return "Store error: \(error)"
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.invalidPresentationContext` to `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (code 2). The branch is compiled only with a Swift 6.4 compiler (Xcode 27).

# What does StoreKitError.networkError mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-network-error.md
Description: StoreKitError.networkError wraps the URLError behind a failed StoreKit 2 request. Read the URLError code, retry once the connection returns, and see how the SDK maps it.

StoreKitError.networkError means a StoreKit 2 request could not finish because of a network problem, and it carries the underlying `URLError`.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.networkError(URLError)` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | A network error occurred. |

## Cause

- A StoreKit 2 request to the App Store failed at the network layer. The case carries a `URLError`, so the real reason (offline, timeout, lost connection) is in its `code`.
- Apple's documentation for the case is one line. The reason is not in the case name; it is in the associated `URLError`.
- The error comes from the device or its connection, not from your app's product configuration.

## Fix

1. Read `urlError.code` first. `.notConnectedToInternet` means the device is offline; `.timedOut` and `.networkConnectionLost` are usually temporary.
2. Retry the action after a short pause, or when the connection returns. Do not retry in a tight loop.
3. Show a message such as "Check your connection and try again" and keep the paywall open.
4. Do not unlock content because of this error. Unlock from verified transactions only.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// A purchase that fails on the network is safe to offer again: nothing was bought.
func buy(_ product: Product) async {
    do {
        let result = try await product.purchase()
        print("Purchase result: \(result)")
    } catch StoreKitError.networkError(let urlError) {
        // The URLError code says why: offline, timeout, lost connection.
        print("Network problem (\(urlError.code.rawValue)); ask the person to try again")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.networkError` to `ErrorCode.networkError` (code 10) and passes the `URLError` along as the underlying error. A device that is offline surfaces as `offlineConnectionError` (code 35) when the SDK's own request fails the same way. See [what networkError means in the SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-network-error.md).

## Related

- [What does networkError (code 10) mean in the purchases SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-network-error.md)
- [What does offlineConnectionError (code 35) mean in the purchases SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-offline-connection-error.md)
- [What does Play Billing NETWORK_ERROR (12) mean?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-network-error.md)

# What does StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-not-available-in-storefront.md
Description: StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront means a StoreKit 2 call is not available on a device whose App Store storefront does not support it. Causes, fix and a Swift example.

StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront means StoreKit 2 refused a function because the device's App Store storefront does not support it.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The function is not available on devices configured for this storefront. |

## Cause

- The device's App Store country or region (its storefront) is one where the requested function is not offered. Apple documents the case in one line and does not publish a list of the calls or storefronts that trigger it.
- In-app products you create in App Store Connect are sold per region, and Apple says you keep your own list of product identifiers and the storefronts where you want them available ([Storefront](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/storefront)).
- In the sandbox, changing the App Store Country or Region of a Sandbox Apple Account changes the storefront your app sees, so a tester can hit this error after a region change ([Storefront](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/storefront)).

## Fix

1. Read the storefront with `Storefront.current` and log its `countryCode` next to the error, so you know which region failed.
2. Check in App Store Connect that the product's availability includes that region, and check the app's own availability too.
3. Do not retry in a loop. The same call fails the same way until the storefront or the availability changes. Hide the product or show a short "not available in your region" message instead.
4. To reproduce it, change the region of a Sandbox Apple Account and run the same call again.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Load products, and explain a storefront problem instead of retrying: the same call keeps failing in that region.
func loadProducts(ids: [String]) async -> [Product] {
    do {
        return try await Product.products(for: ids)
    } catch StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront {
        // Log the region so support can tell a storefront problem from a network problem.
        let region = await Storefront.current?.countryCode ?? "unknown"
        print("StoreKit says this function is not available in storefront \(region)")
        return []
    } catch {
        print("Could not load products: \(error)")
        return []
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork converts `StoreKitError.notAvailableInStorefront` into `ErrorCode.productNotAvailableForPurchaseError` (code 5), the same mapping as the RevenueCat SDK it forks. On Android, Play Billing's `ITEM_UNAVAILABLE` maps to the same code. Read [what productNotAvailableForPurchaseError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-product-not-available-for-purchase-error.md) for the SDK side.

## Related

- [What does productNotAvailableForPurchaseError (code 5) mean in the purchases SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-product-not-available-for-purchase-error.md)
- [What does Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable mean?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-product-unavailable.md)
- [What does Play Billing ITEM_UNAVAILABLE (4) mean?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-item-unavailable.md)

# What does StoreKitError.notEntitled mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-not-entitled.md
Description: StoreKitError.notEntitled means the app lacks the entitlements a StoreKit 2 function needs. What Apple documents, what to check in Xcode and how the SDK maps it.

StoreKitError.notEntitled means the app does not have the entitlements that the StoreKit function it called requires.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.notEntitled` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.4, iPadOS 15.4, macOS 12.3, tvOS 15.4, watchOS 8.5, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The app does not have the appropriate entitlements to use the functionality. |

## Cause

- The app is missing an entitlement that the called StoreKit function requires. Apple documents the case in one line and does not list which functions or entitlements trigger it.
- Apple describes In-App Purchase as a capability: some app services need you to add a capability to the target in Xcode, which can edit the target's entitlements ([Adding capabilities to your app](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/adding-capabilities-to-your-app)).
- The case exists only from iOS 15.4 and macOS 12.3, so older systems report a different failure.

## Fix

1. Open the target's **Signing & Capabilities** tab in Xcode and check that the capabilities your feature needs are present, including In-App Purchase.
2. Confirm the app ID's capabilities in your Apple Developer account match the target, then rebuild and reinstall.
3. If the failing call needs a special entitlement from Apple, request it first; the case name does not say which one.
4. Log the call that threw the error so you can tell which function needed the entitlement.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// notEntitled is an app configuration problem, not a customer problem: log it for yourself and hide the feature.
func syncPurchases() async {
    do {
        try await AppStore.sync()
    } catch StoreKitError.notEntitled {
        print("This build lacks an entitlement for this StoreKit call; check Signing & Capabilities")
    } catch {
        print("Sync failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.notEntitled` to `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (code 2). Because that code also covers temporary store failures, read the underlying error to tell them apart. See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

## Related

- [What does configurationError (code 23) mean in the purchases SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-configuration-error.md)

# What does StoreKitError.systemError mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-system-error.md
Description: StoreKitError.systemError means the system failed a StoreKit 2 call, and it wraps the underlying error. How to read it, what to retry and how the SDK maps it.

StoreKitError.systemError means the operating system reported a failure during a StoreKit 2 call and passes the underlying error along.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.systemError(Error)` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | A system error occurred. |

## Cause

- The system, not your app's request, failed the operation. The case carries the underlying `Error`, which is the only place the detail lives.
- Apple does not list what triggers it. Treat it as a failure outside your code that may be temporary.
- Because the cause is not documented, do not assume a product or configuration problem until the underlying error shows one.

## Fix

1. Log `underlying.localizedDescription` and its `NSError` domain and code, so you can group repeated failures.
2. Retry once after a short pause. If it keeps failing, check that the device has an App Store account signed in and that the App Store app works.
3. Test on a second device or account to separate a device problem from a setup problem.
4. Keep the paywall open and tell the person the store had a problem. Do not unlock content.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// The underlying error is the only detail StoreKit gives you, so log it before you show a generic message.
func refreshProducts(ids: [String]) async {
    do {
        let products = try await Product.products(for: ids)
        print("Loaded \(products.count) products")
    } catch StoreKitError.systemError(let underlying) {
        let ns = underlying as NSError
        print("StoreKit system error: domain \(ns.domain), code \(ns.code), \(ns.localizedDescription)")
    } catch {
        print("Other error: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.systemError` to `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (code 2) and keeps the system error as the underlying error. Retrying once is reasonable; see [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

# What does StoreKitError.unknown mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-unknown.md
Description: StoreKitError.unknown is StoreKit 2's catch-all for an error it cannot name. Log the full error, retry once and see how the purchases SDK reports it.

StoreKitError.unknown is StoreKit 2's catch-all for a failure it has no better name for.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.unknown` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | An unknown error occurred. |

## Cause

- StoreKit raised an error that none of the other `StoreKitError` cases describes. Apple gives no cause, and the case carries no underlying error.
- The RevenueCat SDK source notes that `StoreKitError` does not conform to `CustomNSError` as of iOS 15.2, so no extra detail can be read from it ([StoreKitError+Extensions.swift](https://github.com/revenuedot/purchases-ios/blob/revenuedot/main-patches/Sources/Error%20Handling/StoreKitError%2BExtensions.swift)).
- Because nothing more is known, the cause can be a device problem, a store problem or a configuration problem.

## Fix

1. Log the full error value, the product ID and the iOS version, so repeated cases can be grouped.
2. Retry once after a short pause, and test on a second device and account.
3. Check the basics: the device is signed in to the App Store, the product exists in App Store Connect and the app is the build you think it is.
4. Update to the newest SDK and Xcode, because a case Apple adds later can reach older code as unknown.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// With no detail to read, log everything you have, then show a neutral message.
func buy(_ product: Product) async {
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase()
    } catch StoreKitError.unknown {
        print("StoreKit unknown error for \(product.id) on \(ProcessInfo.processInfo.operatingSystemVersionString)")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.unknown` to `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (code 2), not to `unknownError`. See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md) and [what unknownError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-unknown-error.md).

# What does StoreKitError.unsupported mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-unsupported.md
Description: StoreKitError.unsupported means an operation does not support the product, for example an In-App Purchase not registered as a generic SKU. Cause, fix and example.

StoreKitError.unsupported means the operation you called does not support this product.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.unsupported` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 18.4, iPadOS 18.4, macOS 15.4, tvOS 18.4, watchOS 11.4, visionOS 2.4 |
| What the vendor says | The operation does not support this product. |

## Cause

- Apple says the system raises this error when the type that starts the request does not support the operation. Its example is creating an object with the product ID of an In-App Purchase that is not registered as a generic SKU in App Store Connect.
- The case is new: it exists from iOS 18.4 and macOS 15.4, so you only see it on those systems or later, and only when you build with an Xcode that includes it.
- Apple lists no other trigger, so check the product type before you blame the network.
- Apple's page for the case shows the platform versions above, which is why the SDK guards it behind a newer compiler.

## Fix

1. Check how the product is registered in App Store Connect and whether the API you called is meant for that type of product.
2. Use a different API for the product, or register the product the way the API requires.
3. Build with an Xcode version that knows the case, or the error can arrive in old code as an unknown error.
4. Log the product ID and the call that threw the error.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Raised on iOS 18.4 and later when the call does not support the product; log the ID so you can fix the registration.
func load(ids: [String]) async {
    do {
        let products = try await Product.products(for: ids)
        print("Loaded \(products.count) products")
    } catch StoreKitError.unsupported {
        print("StoreKit says the operation does not support one of these products: \(ids)")
    } catch {
        print("Load failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.unsupported` to `ErrorCode.purchaseInvalidError` (code 4) when it is built with Swift 6.1 or later. See [what purchaseInvalidError means in the SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-invalid-error.md).

# What does StoreKitError.userCancelled mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-error-user-cancelled.md
Description: StoreKitError.userCancelled means the person cancelled a StoreKit 2 flow. It is not a failure: show no error and leave the paywall as it was.

StoreKitError.userCancelled means the person cancelled, so nothing was bought and nothing is broken.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `StoreKitError.userCancelled` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`StoreKitError`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The user canceled. |

## Cause

- The person dismissed a StoreKit flow, such as the purchase confirmation sheet, before finishing it.
- A purchase made with `Product.purchase()` reports a cancel as the result `Product.PurchaseResult.userCancelled`, which Apple documents as the user cancelling the purchase. The error case is the same outcome in error form, so handle both the same way.
- Apple documents no other cause. A cancel is the person's choice, not an App Store failure.

## Fix

1. Do not show an error. A cancel is a normal step in a purchase funnel.
2. Leave the paywall open with its products loaded, so the person can choose again.
3. Count cancels apart from failures in your analytics, so real errors stay visible.
4. Do not unlock anything and do not retry for the person.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Treat a cancel as an outcome, not an error: no alert, no retry, no unlock.
func buy(_ product: Product) async {
    do {
        switch try await product.purchase() {
        case .userCancelled:
            print("Cancelled by the person; leave the paywall as it is")
        case .pending:
            print("Waiting for approval; do not unlock yet")
        case .success(let verification):
            print("Bought: \(verification)")
        @unknown default:
            break
        }
    } catch StoreKitError.userCancelled {
        // The error form of the same outcome.
        print("Cancelled by the person; leave the paywall as it is")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `StoreKitError.userCancelled` to `ErrorCode.purchaseCancelledError` (code 1) and sets `userCancelled` on the purchase result. RevenueDot's server never sees a cancelled purchase, because the SDK stops before it posts a receipt. See [what purchaseCancelledError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-cancelled-error.md).

## Related

- [What does purchaseCancelledError (code 1) mean in the purchases SDK?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-purchase-cancelled-error.md)
- [What does Play Billing USER_CANCELED (1) mean?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/play-billing-user-canceled.md)

# What does Product.PurchaseError.ineligibleForOffer mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-ineligible-for-offer.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.ineligibleForOffer means the customer is not eligible for the offer you applied. Check eligibility before you show an introductory or promotional offer.

Product.PurchaseError.ineligibleForOffer means the customer is not eligible for the offer that the purchase tried to use.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.ineligibleForOffer` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The user is not eligible for the offer. |

## Cause

- Apple says the App Store treats customers with an existing or expired subscription in the app as eligible for a promotional offer. A customer without one is not eligible ([Implementing promotional offers](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/implementing-promotional-offers-in-your-app)).
- Introductory offers have their own rule: `isEligibleForIntroOffer` is true when the customer is eligible for an introductory offer on the subscription or on any subscription in the same group ([isEligibleForIntroOffer](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/subscriptioninfo/iseligibleforintrooffer)).
- A customer who already redeemed the introductory offer in that group is no longer eligible.

## Fix

1. Check eligibility before you show the offer: `Product.SubscriptionInfo.isEligibleForIntroOffer` for introductory offers, and your own rules plus the customer's subscription history for promotional offers.
2. Show the standard price when the customer is not eligible, instead of an offer that will fail.
3. Apple notes that eligibility can be true even when you have not set up an introductory offer, so also check that the offer exists on the product.
4. Do not retry. The result stays the same until the customer's eligibility changes.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Ask the App Store whether this customer can get the introductory offer before you advertise it.
func showPrice(for product: Product) async {
    guard let subscription = product.subscription else { return }
    let eligible = await subscription.isEligibleForIntroOffer
    print(eligible ? "Show the introductory offer" : "Show the standard price")
}

func buy(_ product: Product, options: Set<Product.PurchaseOption>) async {
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase(options: options)
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.ineligibleForOffer {
        print("Not eligible for this offer; fall back to the standard price")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.ineligibleForOffer` to `ErrorCode.ineligibleError` (code 18). See [what ineligibleError means](https://revenuedot.app/errors/ineligible-error) for the SDK side.

# What does Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferIdentifier mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-invalid-offer-identifier.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferIdentifier means the promotional offer ID in the purchase options is not valid. Match it to the offer in App Store Connect.

Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferIdentifier means the promotional offer identifier you passed in the purchase options is not valid.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferIdentifier` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The promotional offer identifier provided in the purchase options is invalid. |

## Cause

- The identifier in `.promotionalOffer(offerID:keyID:nonce:signature:timestamp:)` does not match a promotional offer the App Store knows for this product.
- Apple says promotional offers must first be set up in App Store Connect, and the offers on a product appear in its `subscription.promotionalOffers` array ([promotionalOffer option](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/purchaseoption/promotionaloffer%28offerid:keyid:nonce:signature:timestamp:%29)).
- A typo, an offer attached to another product or an offer you never created all produce this error.

## Fix

1. Read the offer ID from `product.subscription?.promotionalOffers` instead of typing it by hand.
2. Compare the ID with the offer in App Store Connect, character by character.
3. Make sure the offer belongs to the same subscription product you are buying.
4. Sign the offer on your server only after you have picked a valid offer ID, because the ID is part of the signed text.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Take the offer ID from the product itself, so the identifier you sign and send always exists.
func offerID(for product: Product) -> String? {
    product.subscription?.promotionalOffers.first?.id
}

func buy(_ product: Product, options: Set<Product.PurchaseOption>) async {
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase(options: options)
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferIdentifier {
        print("The offer ID is not one of \(product.id)'s promotional offers")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

# What does Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferPrice mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-invalid-offer-price.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferPrice means the App Store says the price of the promotional offer is not valid. Reload the product, check the offer in App Store Connect and try a fresh purchase.

Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferPrice means the App Store judged the price of the offer you tried to apply to be invalid.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferPrice` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The price of the offer isn't valid. |

## Cause

- Apple's case page gives only that one line and lists no causes, so the exact trigger is not documented.
- Apple says promotional offers, with their price, are set up in App Store Connect before the app can use them ([promotionalOffer option](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/purchaseoption/promotionaloffer%28offerid:keyid:nonce:signature:timestamp:%29)). The offer the app applies must be one that still exists there for that product.
- It is a sibling of `invalidOfferIdentifier` and `invalidOfferSignature`: the offer is rejected because of its data, not because the person cancelled or the network failed.

## Fix

1. Read the offer from `product.subscription?.promotionalOffers` after a fresh `Product.products(for:)` call, and show its `displayPrice`, so the price in your UI is the one the App Store holds.
2. Open the offer in App Store Connect and check that it is active for the product and for the storefront the person uses.
3. Do not reuse a signed offer after a failed attempt. Ask your server for a new signature before you try again.
4. Test the same offer in the sandbox. If it fails there too, the offer configuration is the problem, not the device.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Show the price the App Store holds for the offer, and react to the rejection by reloading the product.
func offerPrice(of product: Product, offerID: String) -> String? {
    product.subscription?.promotionalOffers.first { $0.id == offerID }?.displayPrice
}

func buy(_ product: Product, options: Set<Product.PurchaseOption>) async {
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase(options: options)
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferPrice {
        print("The App Store says the offer price is not valid; reload the product and its offers")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferPrice` to `ErrorCode.invalidPromotionalOfferError` (code 34), together with `invalidOfferIdentifier`, `invalidOfferSignature` and `missingOfferParameters`.

# What does Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferSignature mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-invalid-offer-signature.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferSignature means the App Store rejected the signature of a promotional offer. Rebuild the signed text, use a fresh nonce and sign it with the right key.

Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferSignature means the App Store could not validate the signature of the promotional offer.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferSignature` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The offer signature is not valid. |

## Cause

- Apple says the signature is made from the product and offer parameters plus a nonce and timestamp your server generates, joined in a fixed order with the invisible separator U+2063, and signed with your PKCS #8 private key using ECDSA with SHA-256 ([Generating a signature](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/generating-a-signature-for-promotional-offers)).
- Apple also says each payload, signature and nonce is valid for one buy request only, even if the buy fails, so reusing a signature after a failed attempt fails.
- If you pass an app account token, Apple says it must be part of the signed text, and the UUID strings of the token and the nonce must be lowercase ([promotionalOffer option](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/purchaseoption/promotionaloffer%28offerid:keyid:nonce:signature:timestamp:%29)).

## Fix

1. Rebuild the signed string in the exact order Apple lists, with the separator between the parts.
2. Create a new nonce and timestamp for every attempt, and sign again after any failed purchase.
3. Sign with the private key whose key ID you send as `keyID`, and Base64-encode the DER signature.
4. Use lowercase UUID strings for the nonce and the app account token, and sign the same values you send.
5. Check the signature locally with the public key before you send it, as Apple suggests.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// A signature works once. After a failed purchase, ask your server for a new nonce, timestamp and signature.
func buy(_ product: Product, offerID: String, keyID: String, nonce: UUID, signature: Data, timestamp: Int) async {
    let offer = Product.PurchaseOption.promotionalOffer(offerID: offerID, keyID: keyID, nonce: nonce, signature: signature, timestamp: timestamp)
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase(options: [offer])
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferSignature {
        print("The App Store rejected the signature; request a fresh one from the server")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.invalidOfferSignature` to `ErrorCode.invalidPromotionalOfferError` (code 34). The SDK builds and signs the offer for you when you use its promotional offer API, so this error mostly appears when you sign offers yourself.

# What does Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-invalid-quantity.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity means the quantity passed to a StoreKit 2 purchase is not valid. Quantity applies to consumables and non-renewing subscriptions only.

Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity means the quantity you passed to `purchase(options:)` is not valid.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The quantity to purchase is invalid. |

## Cause

- The `.quantity(_:)` purchase option sets how many items the customer buys. Apple says the quantity applies to consumable In-App Purchases and non-renewing subscriptions ([PurchaseOption.quantity](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/purchaseoption/quantity%28_:%29)).
- A quantity for a product of another type, or a value outside what the App Store accepts, is not a valid quantity. Apple does not publish the accepted range on the case page.
- The error comes from the arguments your code passes, so it is reproducible and not a store outage.

## Fix

1. Remove the `.quantity` option unless the product is a consumable or a non-renewing subscription.
2. Pass a whole number of at least 1, and keep it small. Log the value you send.
3. Check the product's type in App Store Connect against what your code assumes.
4. Test the purchase in the sandbox or a StoreKit configuration file before you ship.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Quantity is for consumables and non-renewing subscriptions only; guard the value before you pass it.
func buy(_ product: Product, quantity: Int) async {
    guard quantity >= 1 else { return }
    do {
        let result = try await product.purchase(options: [.quantity(quantity)])
        print("Result: \(result)")
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity {
        print("The App Store rejected quantity \(quantity) for \(product.id)")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.invalidQuantity` to `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (code 2). The SDK's own purchase API does not expose a quantity, so this error normally appears only when your code calls StoreKit directly. See [what storeProblemError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-store-problem-error.md).

# What does Product.PurchaseError.missingOfferParameters mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-missing-offer-parameters.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.missingOfferParameters means the offer parameters are missing from a purchase. Send the offer ID, key ID, nonce, signature and timestamp, or the signed JWS.

Product.PurchaseError.missingOfferParameters means the purchase named an offer but did not carry all the parameters the App Store needs to apply it.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.missingOfferParameters` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The offer parameters are missing. |

## Cause

- Apple's case page gives only that one line. It lists no causes.
- A promotional offer needs several values: the offer ID, and either the key ID, nonce, signature and timestamp from your server, or a compact JWS signed on your server. The `promotionalOffer(offerID:keyID:nonce:signature:timestamp:)` option takes the first group.
- From iOS 26 the signature-and-nonce option is deprecated in the StoreKit interface in favor of `promotionalOffer(_:compactJWS:)`, so apps that mix the two styles can leave a part out.

## Fix

1. Build the offer option from one server response that contains every value, and pass nothing partial.
2. Move to the JWS option (`promotionalOffer(_:compactJWS:)`) when your minimum iOS version allows it. It carries the signed offer as one string.
3. Check that your server returns the key ID, the nonce, the timestamp and the signature, and that the app does not drop one while decoding.
4. Request a fresh signature for each attempt. A signature works for one purchase request only.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Pass every parameter from one server response, so none is missing.
struct SignedOffer {
    let offerID: String
    let keyID: String
    let nonce: UUID
    let signature: Data
    let timestamp: Int
}

func buy(_ product: Product, offer: SignedOffer) async {
    let option = Product.PurchaseOption.promotionalOffer(offerID: offer.offerID, keyID: offer.keyID, nonce: offer.nonce, signature: offer.signature, timestamp: offer.timestamp)
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase(options: [option])
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.missingOfferParameters {
        print("An offer parameter is missing; request a complete signed offer from the server")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.missingOfferParameters` to `ErrorCode.invalidPromotionalOfferError` (code 34). The SDK assembles the offer parameters itself when you use its promotional offer API, so you see this mostly when you build the option by hand.

# What does Product.PurchaseError.paymentMethodBindingConfigurationRequired mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-payment-method-binding-configuration-required.md
Description: paymentMethodBindingConfigurationRequired means the customer must add a payment method to their Apple Account before buying. Use PaymentMethodBinding to prompt them, then retry the purchase.

Product.PurchaseError.paymentMethodBindingConfigurationRequired means the customer has no payment method on their Apple Account, so they must add one before the purchase can go through.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.paymentMethodBindingConfigurationRequired` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 26.5, iPadOS 26.5, macOS 26.5, tvOS 26.5, watchOS 26.5, visionOS 26.5 |
| What the vendor says | The customer needs to add a payment method to their Apple Account before making a purchase; use PaymentMethodBinding to prompt the customer and bind the payment method. |

## Cause

- Apple says the customer has no usable payment method on their Apple Account at the time of the purchase.
- `PaymentMethodBinding` is available only to eligible apps with server entitlements. Its initializer throws if the app lacks the entitlement or the person is not eligible ([PaymentMethodBinding](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/paymentmethodbinding)).
- The error exists from iOS 26.5, so older systems never throw it.

## Fix

1. Catch the error and start the binding flow: your server asks Apple for an in-app binding identifier, the app creates `PaymentMethodBinding(id:)` with it and calls `bind()`.
2. `bind()` shows the system prompt where the customer confirms the new payment method as their primary one. Retry the purchase when it returns.
3. If the initializer throws, the app or the customer is not eligible. Show a message that points to Settings and the Apple Account payment methods instead.
4. Guard the code with an availability check for iOS 26.5 and keep a generic error path for earlier versions.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// When the customer has no payment method, bind one with the identifier your server got from Apple, then buy again.
@available(iOS 26.5, *)
func buy(_ product: Product, bindingID: () async -> String?) async {
    do {
        _ = try await product.purchase()
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.paymentMethodBindingConfigurationRequired {
        guard let id = await bindingID() else { return }
        do {
            let binding = try await PaymentMethodBinding(id: id)
            try await binding.bind()
            print("Payment method bound; buy again")
        } catch {
            print("Binding failed: \(error)")
        }
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

## How the RevenueDot SDK reports it

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.paymentMethodBindingConfigurationRequired` to `ErrorCode.storeProblemError` (code 2). The branch is compiled only with Xcode 26.5 or newer. The SDK does not start the binding flow for you.

# What does Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/storekit-purchase-error-product-unavailable.md
Description: Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable means the product cannot be bought. Check its state in App Store Connect, its availability by region and its identifier.

Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable means the App Store reports that this product is not available to buy.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Error | `Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable` |
| Where | StoreKit 2, Swift (`Product.purchase(options:)`) |
| Available since | iOS 15.0, iPadOS 15.0, macOS 12.0, tvOS 15.0, watchOS 8.0, visionOS 1.0 |
| What the vendor says | The product is not available. |

## Cause

- The App Store has the product but will not sell it to this customer right now. Apple's page for the case gives no further reason.
- Apple notes that if an identifier is invalid or the App Store cannot find it, `Product.products(for:)` leaves it out of the result instead of throwing ([products(for:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/products%28for:%29)). A product you hold but cannot buy is a different state from one that never loaded.
- Products are sold per region, and Apple tells developers to keep their own list of identifiers and the storefronts where they are available ([Storefront](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/storefront)).

## Fix

1. Check the product in App Store Connect: it must exist, have complete metadata and be available in the customer's region.
2. Compare the identifier in your code character by character with the one in App Store Connect.
3. Reload products and compare the IDs you asked for with the IDs that came back, to see which one is missing.
4. Hide or disable the buy button for the product until it loads, and do not retry the same call in a loop.

## Example

```swift
import StoreKit

// Compare what you asked for with what came back, so a missing product is a log line instead of a silent dead button.
func buy(id: String) async {
    do {
        guard let product = try await Product.products(for: [id]).first else {
            print("The App Store returned no product for \(id); check the identifier and availability")
            return
        }
        _ = try await product.purchase()
    } catch Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable {
        print("\(id) exists but cannot be bought right now")
    } catch {
        print("Purchase failed: \(error)")
    }
}
```

*Compile-checked: `npm run check:snippets` type-checks this snippet with `swiftc` against the Apple SDK (macOS target, checked 2026-10-03).*

The RevenueDot `purchases-ios` fork maps `Product.PurchaseError.productUnavailable` to `ErrorCode.productNotAvailableForPurchaseError` (code 5). In RevenueDot, make sure the product's store identifier equals the App Store identifier. See [what productNotAvailableForPurchaseError means](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/errors/sdk-product-not-available-for-purchase-error.md).
