# What does the App Store notification SUBSCRIBED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/apple-subscribed.md
Description: SUBSCRIBED means a customer subscribed to an auto-renewable subscription. Subtype INITIAL_BUY is the first time, RESUBSCRIBE a return. Grant access and record the purchase.

The App Store notification SUBSCRIBED means a customer subscribed to an auto-renewable subscription, for the first time or again.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `notificationType` `SUBSCRIBED` |
| Where | App Store Server Notifications v2 (`responseBodyV2DecodedPayload`) |
| Sent by | The App Store server, to your notification URL |
| What Apple says | The customer subscribed to an auto-renewable subscription. The subtype says whether it is the first purchase or a resubscribe. |

## What triggers it

- Subtype `INITIAL_BUY`: the customer bought or got access through Family Sharing to a subscription in the group for the first time, including by redeeming an offer code.
- Subtype `RESUBSCRIBE`: the customer resubscribed, or got access through Family Sharing, to the same subscription or another one in the same subscription group, including through a promotional, offer code or win-back offer.
- To tell whether an offer was used, Apple says to check `offerType` in the decoded transaction (`JWSTransactionDecodedPayload`).

## What your server should do

1. Verify the `signedPayload` with Apple's App Store Server Library (`SignedDataVerifier.verifyAndDecodeNotification`) before you act on anything in it.
2. Decode `signedTransactionInfo`, find the customer through your own account link (for example the `appAccountToken`) and grant the entitlement until `expiresDate`.
3. Treat `RESUBSCRIBE` as access again, not as a second first purchase, so your counts of new subscribers stay right.
4. Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).

## Example

```javascript
// Run on the decoded payload, after you verified Apple's signature.
const notification = {"notificationType":"SUBSCRIBED","data":{"environment":"Sandbox","bundleId":"com.example.app"}};

function decide(n) {
  if (n.notificationType !== "SUBSCRIBED") return "ignore";
  return n.subtype === "RESUBSCRIBE" ? "grant access, count a returning subscriber" : "grant access, count a new subscriber";
}

console.log(decide(notification));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `count a new subscriber` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. `SUBSCRIBED` is one of the types that update the stored purchase from the signed transaction and renewal info. A chain RevenueDot has not stored before produces `INITIAL_PURCHASE`; a chain it already holds with a new period produces `RENEWAL`, because RevenueCat reports a lapsed customer who resubscribes as a renewal and RevenueDot copies that. The subtype is not used; the stored state is.

# What does the App Store notification TEST mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/apple-test.md
Description: TEST is the notification the App Store sends when you ask for one with the Request a Test Notification endpoint. Use it to check your server receives and answers notifications.

The App Store notification TEST is a sample notification that Apple sends only when you request it, to check that your server receives notifications.

## Quick facts

| Notification | `notificationType` `TEST` |
| Where | App Store Server Notifications v2 (`responseBodyV2DecodedPayload`) |
| Sent by | The App Store server, to your notification URL |
| What Apple says | The App Store server sends it when you call the Request a Test Notification endpoint. You get it only at your request. |

## What triggers it

- You called Request a Test Notification in the App Store Server API,.
- It carries no purchase, so there is nothing to apply.

3. Do not treat it as a customer event.
4. If it does not arrive, call Get Test Notification Status for the failure reason.
5. Answer HTTP 200 (any code from 200 to 206) once you have stored the notification. Apple retries other answers five times, at 1, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours after the previous attempt, so make your handler safe to run twice (the payload carries a `notificationUUID`).

```javascript
// Run on the decoded payload, after you verified Apple's signature.
const notification = {"notificationType":"TEST","data":{"environment":"Sandbox","bundleId":"com.example.app"}};

  return "answer 200, do not touch any customer";
}

console.log(decide(notification));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `answer 200` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot verifies Apple's signature, checks the bundle ID, stores the notification and answers 200. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores the test notification, answers 200 and counts it as received, so the app's notification status in setup health can turn ready. It applies nothing and sends no webhook event.

# What does the Google Play notification ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_CANCELED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-one-time-product-canceled.md
Description: ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_CANCELED (2) means a pending one-time purchase was cancelled by the customer. Nothing was delivered, so drop any pending record.

The Google Play notification ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_CANCELED means a customer cancelled a one-time purchase that was still pending.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `oneTimeProductNotification.notificationType` 2, `ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_CANCELED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A pending one-time product purchase has been canceled by the user. |

## What triggers it

- The customer started a purchase with a delayed payment method and cancelled before it finished.
- It is about a pending purchase only. A refund of a completed purchase arrives as a voided purchase notification.
- Like the purchase type, it is sent only when you enabled one-time product events.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Drop any pending record for that token and `sku`.
3. Do not deliver the item.
4. Do not confuse it with a refund: use the voided purchase notification for those.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","oneTimeProductNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":2,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN","sku":"coins_100"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.oneTimeProductNotification?.notificationType === 2)) return "ignore";
  return "drop the pending purchase, deliver nothing";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `deliver nothing` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot ignores it: the message is stored and answered 2xx with status `ignored`, and only type 1 (purchased) is applied. Refunds come through the voided purchase notification.

# What does the Google Play notification ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_PURCHASED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-one-time-product-purchased.md
Description: ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_PURCHASED (1) means a one-time product was bought. Fetch the purchase, deliver the item once and acknowledge or consume it.

The Google Play notification ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_PURCHASED means a customer bought a one-time product.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `oneTimeProductNotification.notificationType` 1, `ONE_TIME_PRODUCT_PURCHASED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A one-time product was successfully purchased by a user. |

## What triggers it

- A customer completed the purchase of an in-app product.
- Google sends it only if you chose to receive one-time product purchase events when you set up notifications.
- The message carries the `sku` and the `purchaseToken`.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Call the products API with the `sku` and token, check the purchase state, and deliver the item once.
3. Acknowledge or consume the purchase so Google does not refund it.
4. Key delivery on the order so a repeat message does not give the item twice.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","oneTimeProductNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":1,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN","sku":"coins_100"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.oneTimeProductNotification?.notificationType === 1)) return "ignore";
  return "verify, deliver once, acknowledge";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `deliver once` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot fetches the product purchase for the `sku` and token, skips a purchase that is still pending, stores it under its order ID and acknowledges it. A new purchase gives `NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE`. The consumable flag comes from the product's type in your catalog.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-canceled.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED (3) means a subscription was cancelled by the customer, you or the system. Access continues to the expiry time; do not remove it early.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED means a subscription was cancelled, but the customer keeps access until the paid period ends.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 3, `SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription was cancelled, voluntarily or involuntarily. For a voluntary cancellation, it is sent when the user cancels. |

## What triggers it

- The customer cancelled in the Play subscriptions center, you cancelled with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.cancel`, or the subscription was cancelled after account hold ran out.
- The subscription resource then has `subscriptionState` `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_CANCELED`, and `expiryTime` says when access ends. If that time is already past, for example after a cancel during account hold, access ends now.
- `canceledStateContext` says who cancelled and `userInitiatedCancellation` can say why.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Keep access until `expiryTime`. Google warns that removing access a customer is still entitled to violates its subscriptions policy.
3. Show a message with the end date and a way to resubscribe.
4. Read `canceledStateContext` to choose your win-back message.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":3,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 3)) return "ignore";
  return "keep access until expiryTime, show the end date";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `keep access until expiryTime` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores the purchase as unsubscribed and sends `CANCELLATION`. The `cancel_reason` is `DEVELOPER_INITIATED` when Google says you cancelled it, `BILLING_ERROR` or `PRICE_INCREASE` when the system did, and `UNSUBSCRIBE` otherwise. A cancellation caused by an upgrade or downgrade is not a customer cancellation and is skipped. The `EXPIRATION` event comes later.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-deferred.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED (9) means a subscription's billing date was pushed later with the defer API. The customer keeps full access and is not charged during the deferral.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED means the billing date of a subscription was moved later, so the customer gets more time without a charge.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 9, `SUBSCRIPTION_DEFERRED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription's recurrence time has been extended. |

## What triggers it

- Your backend called `purchases.subscriptionsv2.defer`, for example for a free week as a promotion or a goodwill gesture.
- During the deferral the customer has full access and is not charged. The renewal date is updated.
- For prepaid plans the defer API moves the expiration time.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Store the new `expiryTime` and extend access to it.
3. Record why the deferral was given, so support can explain it.
4. Do not treat it as a payment.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":9,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 9)) return "ignore";
  return "extend access to the new expiryTime, no payment";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `no payment` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. The period start is unchanged and the end moves later, so RevenueDot sends `SUBSCRIPTION_EXTENDED`. No money moves on it: its `price` is 0.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-expired.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED (13) means a subscription has expired. Confirm the state is expired, then remove the entitlement.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED means a subscription has run out and the customer should lose access.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 13, `SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription has expired. |

## What triggers it

- The paid period ended after a cancellation, or account hold ran out.
- The subscription resource has `subscriptionState` `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_EXPIRED` and `expiryTime` in the past.
- A revoked subscription also reads as expired.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Confirm `subscriptionState` is `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_EXPIRED`, then remove the entitlement.
3. Mark the purchase as no longer valid in your backend.
4. Keep the customer's data, since they can resubscribe, which is a new purchase.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":13,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 13)) return "ignore";
  return "confirm the state, remove the entitlement";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `remove the entitlement` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores the purchase as ended and as unsubscribed (a `CANCELLATION` if none had been sent). The `EXPIRATION` event is recorded once by the scheduler when access, grace included, has ended, with the reason from the stored state.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-in-grace-period.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD (6) means a renewal payment failed and the subscription entered its grace period. Keep access and prompt the customer to fix payment.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD means a renewal payment failed, but the customer keeps access during the grace period.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 6, `SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription has entered the grace period, if the grace period is enabled. |

## What triggers it

- A renewal payment failed and the base plan has a grace period. Google enables it by default on auto-renewing base plans.
- Google waits at least one day before the notification even with a grace period of zero days, to leave time for payment retries.
- The subscription resource has state `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_IN_GRACE_PERIOD` and `expiryTime` stays in the past until the grace period ends, but entitlement should last.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Keep access while the grace period runs.
3. Encourage the customer to fix their payment method, with a message in your app.
4. Expect `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` or `SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED` on success, or `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` when the grace period ends.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":6,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 6)) return "ignore";
  return "keep access, show a fix-payment message";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `keep access` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores a billing issue with the grace period end set to the line item's expiry, so access continues. It sends `BILLING_ISSUE` with `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` and a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`. If access later ends, `EXPIRATION` follows.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-on-hold.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD (5) means a subscription entered account hold after a payment failure. Block access and ask the customer to fix their payment method.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD means a renewal payment failed and the subscription is now in account hold, so access should stop.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 5, `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription has entered account hold, if account hold is enabled. |

## What triggers it

- A renewal payment failed and any grace period has ended. Account hold then begins. Google's default is 60 days minus the grace period.
- A subscription resuming from a pause with a failed payment goes straight into account hold.
- During hold the `expiryTime` stays in the past and the customer should not have access.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Block access to the subscription while it is on hold.
3. Ask the customer to fix their payment method. Google tells customers too.
4. When they do, you get `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` with the same purchase token. If they do not, the subscription is cancelled and expires.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 5)) return "ignore";
  return "block access, ask the customer to fix their payment method";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot stores a billing issue and ends access now. It sends `BILLING_ISSUE` and a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`, and the scheduler sends `EXPIRATION` with `expiration_reason: BILLING_ERROR`. A recovery later comes out as `RENEWAL`.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSE_SCHEDULE_CHANGED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-pause-schedule-changed.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSE_SCHEDULE_CHANGED (11) means a customer scheduled or changed a pause. Access continues until the next renewal date; the pause starts then.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSE_SCHEDULE_CHANGED means a customer set or changed a pause that starts at the end of the current period.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 11, `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSE_SCHEDULE_CHANGED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription pause schedule has been changed. |

## What triggers it

- The customer chose to pause in Play. A pause takes effect only after the current billing period ends.
- The subscription is still `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_ACTIVE` and `autoRenewEnabled` is true. The customer keeps access until the next renewal date.
- Pause lengths run from one week to three months depending on the recurrence.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Keep access until the renewal date and show that a pause is coming.
3. When the pause starts, you get `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED`.
4. Offer a way to resume by deep link to Google Play.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":11,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 11)) return "ignore";
  return "keep access until the renewal date, show the coming pause";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `keep access until the renewal date` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot reads the scheduled resume time from the version 1 subscription API and stores it as the auto-resume date while the subscription is still active. A newly set resume date gives `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED` with `auto_resume_at_ms`, at scheduling time, while access continues.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-paused.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED (10) means a subscription's pause took effect. Remove access until it resumes; the resume time is in the paused state context.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED means a subscription's pause has started, so the customer should have no access until it resumes.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 10, `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription has been paused. |

## What triggers it

- The pause the customer scheduled has reached the end of the paid period and now takes effect.
- The subscription resource has state `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_PAUSED`, with `autoRenewEnabled` true. The `pausedStateContext` says when it renews again.
- While paused the customer has no access and pays nothing.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Remove access until the subscription resumes.
3. Show the expected resume date from `pausedStateContext`.
4. Wait for `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` when it resumes, or `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` if the payment fails on resume.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.

  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 10)) return "ignore";
  return "remove access until it resumes, show the resume date";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `remove access until it resumes` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot ends access now, stores the auto-resume date from the paused state and keeps the scheduled date. The scheduler then sends `EXPIRATION` with `expiration_reason: SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED`.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PENDING_PURCHASE_CANCELED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-pending-purchase-canceled.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_PENDING_PURCHASE_CANCELED (20) means a pending subscription purchase was cancelled before it completed. Nothing was granted, so remove any pending state.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PENDING_PURCHASE_CANCELED means a purchase that was still pending was cancelled before it went through.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 20, `SUBSCRIPTION_PENDING_PURCHASE_CANCELED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A pending transaction of a subscription has been canceled. |

## What triggers it

- The customer started a purchase with a slow payment method, and it was cancelled before completing.
- The subscription never became active, so no access was ever due.
- Pending purchases are shown by Google as `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_PENDING` until they finish.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Remove any pending marker you kept for this purchase token.
3. Do not grant access and do not acknowledge the purchase.
4. Let the customer try again.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":20,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 20)) return "ignore";
  return "drop the pending purchase, grant nothing";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `grant nothing` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot ignores it: the message is stored, answered 2xx with status `ignored`, and no purchase or event is created. Pending subscription states are ignored the same way.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-purchased.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED (4) means a new subscription was purchased. Fetch its state, grant access and acknowledge it within three days or Google refunds it.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED means a new subscription was purchased and has a new purchase token.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 4, `SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A new subscription was purchased. |

## What triggers it

- A customer bought a subscription in your app or in the Play Store.
- A resubscribe after the old subscription expired is a new purchase with a brand new purchase token and no `linkedPurchaseToken`.
- An upgrade, downgrade or signup after cancelling from your app creates a new token with `linkedPurchaseToken` pointing to the old one.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Call `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`, check `subscriptionState` is `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_ACTIVE`, and grant access.
3. Acknowledge the purchase within three days. Google says an unacknowledged purchase is refunded and revoked automatically.
4. Use `linkedPurchaseToken` or `outOfAppPurchaseContext` to connect the new token to the right customer.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":4,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 4)) return "ignore";
  return "fetch the subscription, grant access, acknowledge within three days";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `acknowledge within three days` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A token RevenueDot has not stored gives an `INITIAL_PURCHASE` event; a replacement token joins the customer of its `linkedPurchaseToken`, and the old chain ends with a `PRODUCT_CHANGE` event instead of a `CANCELLATION` or `EXPIRATION`. RevenueDot acknowledges the purchase itself, and if that fails it answers 5xx so Pub/Sub retries.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-recovered.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED (1) means a subscription recovered from account hold or resumed from a pause. Restore access and extend it to the new expiry time.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED means a subscription came back from account hold or from a pause.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 1, `SUBSCRIPTION_RECOVERED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription was recovered from account hold or resumed from a pause. |

## What triggers it

- The customer fixed their payment method during account hold, and the retried payment worked. The purchase token stays the same.
- A paused subscription resumed, at the end of the pause or because the customer resumed it by hand.
- The billing date moves to the recovery date.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Restore access and extend it to the new `expiryTime`.
3. Remove any fix-payment or paused message in your app.
4. Do not count it as a new subscriber.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":1,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 1)) return "ignore";
  return "restore access, extend to the new expiryTime";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `restore access` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A new order on a token whose access had ended is Google renewing it, so RevenueDot moves the stored end to now and sends `RENEWAL`, not a new purchase and not `UNCANCELLATION`.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-renewed.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED (2) means an active subscription renewed. Fetch the new expiry time and extend access. Renewals need no acknowledgement.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED means an active subscription renewed for another period.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 2, `SUBSCRIPTION_RENEWED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | An active subscription was renewed. |

## What triggers it

- The renewal charge succeeded on the billing date.
- For installment subscriptions, Google sends it each time a payment is charged on its billing date.
- Renewals do not need to be acknowledged.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Check the customer is still entitled, then store the new `expiryTime` from the subscription resource.
3. Do not acknowledge a renewal: Google says it is not needed.
4. Keep the order ID (`latestOrderId`), which is new for every renewal.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":2,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 2)) return "ignore";
  return "extend access to the new expiryTime";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `extend access` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. A new order on the token gives a `RENEWAL` event, with `is_trial_conversion: true` when the previous period was a free trial. Renewal order IDs carry a `..N` suffix, which is how RevenueDot tells a renewal order from the first.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-restarted.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED (7) means the customer restored a cancelled subscription from Play before it expired. It keeps its purchase token and renews again.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED means a customer undid a cancellation before the subscription expired.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 7, `SUBSCRIPTION_RESTARTED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | The user restored their subscription from Play, Account, Subscriptions. The subscription was cancelled but had not expired when the user restored it. |

## What triggers it

- The customer tapped Resubscribe on a cancelled subscription that was still running. Google calls this a restore.
- The same purchase token continues and all cancellation fields are cleared.
- After expiry the same action is a new purchase and arrives as `SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED`.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Record that the subscription is set to renew again and stop showing restore messages.
3. Do not grant anything new: the customer already has access until `expiryTime`.
4. Stop your win-back flow for this customer.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":7,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 7)) return "ignore";
  return "mark as renewing, stop restore messages";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `mark as renewing` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. The cancellation is cleared on the stored purchase and RevenueDot sends `UNCANCELLATION`.

# What does the Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-subscription-revoked.md
Description: SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED (12) means a subscription was revoked before its expiry, for example by you or by a chargeback. Remove access at once.

The Google Play notification SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED means a subscription was taken away before its expiration time, so access must end now.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `subscriptionNotification.notificationType` 12, `SUBSCRIPTION_REVOKED` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A subscription has been revoked from the user before the expiration time. |

## What triggers it

- Your backend revoked it with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.revoke`, or the purchase was charged back.
- The subscription resource has `subscriptionState` set to `SUBSCRIPTION_STATE_EXPIRED`.
- Unlike a cancellation, the customer does not keep access to the period end.

## What your server should do

1. Do not trust the message for the state. Google says a notification only tells you the purchase state changed; call the Google Play Developer API (`purchases.subscriptionsv2.get`) with the purchase token to get the full state.
2. Revoke the customer's entitlement immediately.
3. Record the revocation for support and refund reports.
4. Offer a new subscription if the revocation was in error.
5. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","subscriptionNotification":{"version":"1.0","notificationType":12,"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN"}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.subscriptionNotification?.notificationType === 12)) return "ignore";
  return "revoke access immediately";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `revoke access immediately` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. RevenueDot marks the current period refunded at the event time and cuts its expiry to that time. It sends `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price, the same as a refund. If Google no longer knows the token, it refunds from what it stored.

# What does the Google Play notification VOIDED_PURCHASE mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/notifications/google-voided-purchase.md
Description: A voidedPurchaseNotification means Google voided a purchase: a refund, chargeback or revocation. Revoke the item or access using the order ID and refund type.

A Google Play voidedPurchaseNotification means a purchase was voided, usually by a refund or a chargeback, so what it granted should be taken back.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Notification | `voidedPurchaseNotification` |
| Where | Google Play real-time developer notifications (Pub/Sub, `DeveloperNotification`) |
| Sent by | Google Play, as a Cloud Pub/Sub push to your endpoint |
| What Google says | A purchase has been voided. The message gives the purchase token, the order ID, the product type (subscription or one-time) and the refund type (full or quantity-based partial). |

## What triggers it

- The customer was refunded, charged back, or you revoked the purchase.
- `productType` 1 is a subscription and 2 a one-time product. `refundType` 1 is a full refund and 2 a quantity-based partial refund of a multi-quantity purchase.
- For subscriptions, a new order ID is created for each renewal, so the order ID says which period was voided.

## What your server should do

1. Find the purchase by `purchaseToken` and `orderId` and revoke what that order granted.
2. For a partial refund, adjust the quantity instead of revoking everything. `refundableQuantity` in the products API gives what is left.
3. For more data, use Google's Voided Purchases API, a pull model over a time range.
4. Answer 2xx once you have handled the message, and skip a `messageId` you have seen: Google recommends checking the uniqueness of message IDs so a redelivery does not make a second API call.

## Example

```javascript
// A Pub/Sub push body: the notification is base64 JSON in message.data.
const body = { message: { messageId: "136969346945", data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({"version":"1.0","packageName":"com.example.app","eventTimeMillis":"1790800914000","voidedPurchaseNotification":{"purchaseToken":"PURCHASE_TOKEN","orderId":"GPA.1234-5678-9012-34567","productType":1,"refundType":1}})).toString("base64") } };

function decide(body) {
  const n = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(body.message.data, "base64").toString("utf8"));
  if (!(n.voidedPurchaseNotification)) return "ignore";
  const v = n.voidedPurchaseNotification;
  if (v.refundType === 2) return "reduce the quantity, keep the purchase";
  return v.productType === 1 ? "revoke the subscription period of this order" : "revoke the one-time item";
}

console.log(decide(body));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `revoke the subscription period` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot handles it

RevenueDot answers every handled message with 2xx and every temporary failure with 5xx so Pub/Sub redelivers it. For subscription types it re-reads the subscription from Google with `purchases.subscriptionsv2.get` and applies that state, and it acknowledges a new purchase if the app has not. A purchase RevenueDot has not seen is applied only when the app's **Track new purchases from server-to-server notifications** setting is on. For a subscription RevenueDot marks the voided period refunded (only if the order is the current one) and sends `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price. A one-time purchase is marked refunded the same way. A partial quantity refund (`refundType` 2) of a one-time product is ignored. A daily scan of Google's voided purchases catches refunds whose message never arrived.

# What does the RevenueDot webhook event BILLING_ISSUE mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/webhooks/webhook-billing-issue.md
Description: BILLING_ISSUE is sent when a renewal charge fails. The store retries and access may continue in a grace period. Prompt the customer to fix their payment method.

The RevenueDot webhook event BILLING_ISSUE means a subscription's renewal payment failed and the store is retrying it.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Event | `BILLING_ISSUE` |
| Where | RevenueDot webhook (`event.type`), RevenueCat's webhook format |
| Sent to | Every enabled webhook whose filters match |
| Fields that are specific to it | `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` |
| What it means | A renewal charge failed. The store retries; access may continue in a grace period. |

## When it is sent

- The store could not charge the customer's payment method at renewal.
- `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` is always present and is null when there is no grace period.
- RevenueDot also sends a `CANCELLATION` with `cancel_reason: BILLING_ERROR`, as RevenueCat does.

## What your server should do

1. Keep access until `grace_period_expiration_at_ms` when it is set, otherwise follow the store's guidance for your app.
2. Ask the customer to update their payment method.
3. Expect `RENEWAL` if billing recovers, or `EXPIRATION` with `BILLING_ERROR` if the store gives up.
4. Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

## Example

```javascript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">
function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const m = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header ?? "");
  if (!m || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(m[1])) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${m[1]}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, Buffer.from(m[2], "hex"));
}

// Sign a sample delivery the way RevenueDot does, then handle it.
const secret = "whsec_test_secret";
const rawBody = JSON.stringify({ api_version: "1.0", event: {"id":"66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2","type":"BILLING_ISSUE","app_user_id":"user_1","product_id":"pro_monthly","grace_period_expiration_at_ms":1790900000000} });
const t = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const header = `t=${t},v1=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex")}`;

const seen = new Set(); // use a database table in production

function handle(rawBody, header) {
  if (!verify(rawBody, header, secret)) return "401 bad signature";
  const { event } = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  if (seen.has(event.id)) return "200 duplicate";
  seen.add(event.id);
  if (event.type !== "BILLING_ISSUE") return "200 ignored";
  const grace = event.grace_period_expiration_at_ms;
  return grace ? "keep access until " + new Date(grace).toISOString().slice(0, 10) + ", ask to fix payment" : "ask to fix payment";
}

console.log(handle(rawBody, header));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `ask to fix payment` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot produces it

`diffSubscription` returns `BILLING_ISSUE` when a billing issue time appears on the stored purchase. Apple's `DID_FAIL_TO_RENEW` and Google's `SUBSCRIPTION_IN_GRACE_PERIOD` and `SUBSCRIPTION_ON_HOLD` all set it.

# What does the RevenueDot webhook event CANCELLATION mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/webhooks/webhook-cancellation.md
Description: CANCELLATION is sent when auto-renew is turned off or a purchase is refunded. Access continues to the expiry time unless it was a refund. Check cancel_reason.

The RevenueDot webhook event CANCELLATION means a subscription will not renew, or a purchase was refunded.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Event | `CANCELLATION` |
| Where | RevenueDot webhook (`event.type`), RevenueCat's webhook format |
| Sent to | Every enabled webhook whose filters match |
| Fields that are specific to it | `cancel_reason` |
| What it means | Auto-renew was turned off, or the purchase was refunded. Access continues to `expiration_at_ms` unless it was a refund. A refund has `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative price. |

## When it is sent

- The customer turned auto-renew off (`cancel_reason: UNSUBSCRIBE`), the store gave a reason such as `DEVELOPER_INITIATED` or `PRICE_INCREASE`, or a billing failure counted as a cancellation (`BILLING_ERROR`).
- A refund gives `cancel_reason: CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` and a negative `price`.
- It is not the end of access. `EXPIRATION` follows when the paid period ends.

## What your server should do

1. For an unsubscribe, keep access until `expiration_at_ms` and start your win-back flow.
2. For `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT` with a negative price, revoke access now.
3. Use `cancel_reason` to separate voluntary from billing-related churn.
4. Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

## Example

```javascript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">
function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const m = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header ?? "");
  if (!m || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(m[1])) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${m[1]}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, Buffer.from(m[2], "hex"));
}

// Sign a sample delivery the way RevenueDot does, then handle it.
const secret = "whsec_test_secret";
const rawBody = JSON.stringify({ api_version: "1.0", event: {"id":"66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2","type":"CANCELLATION","app_user_id":"user_1","product_id":"pro_monthly","cancel_reason":"UNSUBSCRIBE"} });
const t = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const header = `t=${t},v1=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex")}`;

const seen = new Set(); // use a database table in production

function handle(rawBody, header) {
  if (!verify(rawBody, header, secret)) return "401 bad signature";
  const { event } = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  if (seen.has(event.id)) return "200 duplicate";
  seen.add(event.id);
  if (event.type !== "CANCELLATION") return "200 ignored";
  if (event.cancel_reason === "CUSTOMER_SUPPORT") return "revoke access now, book the refund";
  return "keep access until expiration_at_ms, start win-back";
}

console.log(handle(rawBody, header));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `keep access until expiration_at_ms` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot produces it

`diffSubscription` returns `CANCELLATION` when auto-renew goes off (with the reason from the store, or `BILLING_ERROR` when a billing issue is stored, else `UNSUBSCRIBE`) and, with `isRefund`, when a refund time appears (reason `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`). One-time purchases get the refund form too.

# What does the RevenueDot webhook event EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/webhooks/webhook-experiment-enrollment.md
Description: EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT is sent once per customer and experiment when a customer joins an offering experiment. It carries no app, so app-scoped webhooks do not get it.

The RevenueDot webhook event EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT means a customer joined an offering experiment.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Event | `EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT` |
| Where | RevenueDot webhook (`event.type`), RevenueCat's webhook format |
| Sent to | Every enabled webhook whose filters match |
| Fields that are specific to it | `experiment_id`, `experiment_variant`, `offering_id`, `experiment_enrolled_at_ms` |
| What it means | A customer joined an offering experiment: the first offerings request that enrolled them. Sent once per customer and experiment, as a production event with no app. |

## When it is sent

- The first offerings request of a customer that matches an experiment's targeting enrolls them in a variant.
- It is sent once per customer and experiment.
- It is a production event with no app, so a webhook set to sandbox only, or to one app, does not get it.

## What your server should do

1. Store the `experiment_id` and `experiment_variant` (`a` is the control) against the customer so your analytics can split results.
2. Do not use it to grant anything.
3. Use a webhook set to production and all apps if you need it.
4. Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

## Example

```javascript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">
function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const m = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header ?? "");
  if (!m || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(m[1])) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${m[1]}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, Buffer.from(m[2], "hex"));
}

// Sign a sample delivery the way RevenueDot does, then handle it.
const secret = "whsec_test_secret";
const rawBody = JSON.stringify({ api_version: "1.0", event: {"id":"66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2","type":"EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT","app_user_id":"user_1","product_id":"pro_monthly","experiment_id":"exp_1","experiment_variant":"b"} });
const t = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const header = `t=${t},v1=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex")}`;

const seen = new Set(); // use a database table in production

function handle(rawBody, header) {
  if (!verify(rawBody, header, secret)) return "401 bad signature";
  const { event } = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  if (seen.has(event.id)) return "200 duplicate";
  seen.add(event.id);
  if (event.type !== "EXPERIMENT_ENROLLMENT") return "200 ignored";
  return "record " + event.app_user_id + " in " + event.experiment_id + " variant " + event.experiment_variant;
}

console.log(handle(rawBody, header));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `variant b` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot produces it

`services/targeting.ts` records it with `recordRawEvent` in the experiment shape (no `app_id`, no subscriber attributes) the first time a customer is enrolled.

# What does the RevenueDot webhook event EXPIRATION mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/webhooks/webhook-expiration.md
Description: EXPIRATION is sent when access ended: the period ran out, billing retry gave up, or the subscription paused. Remove access and read expiration_reason.

The RevenueDot webhook event EXPIRATION means a customer's access has ended.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Event | `EXPIRATION` |
| Where | RevenueDot webhook (`event.type`), RevenueCat's webhook format |
| Sent to | Every enabled webhook whose filters match |
| Fields that are specific to it | `expiration_reason` |
| What it means | Access ended: the period ran out, billing retry gave up or the subscription paused. |

## When it is sent

- The paid period, and any grace period, passed with no renewal.
- `expiration_reason` says why: `UNSUBSCRIBE`, `BILLING_ERROR`, `DEVELOPER_INITIATED`, `PRICE_INCREASE`, `CUSTOMER_SUPPORT`, `UNKNOWN` or `SUBSCRIPTION_PAUSED`.
- It is recorded once per period by a scheduled job that runs every minute, so it can arrive up to a minute after the expiry time.

## What your server should do

1. Remove the entitlements of the subscription.
2. Use `expiration_reason` to choose the win-back message: a billing error needs a payment prompt.
3. Keep the customer's data.
4. Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

## Example

```javascript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">
function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const m = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header ?? "");
  if (!m || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(m[1])) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${m[1]}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, Buffer.from(m[2], "hex"));
}

// Sign a sample delivery the way RevenueDot does, then handle it.
const secret = "whsec_test_secret";
const rawBody = JSON.stringify({ api_version: "1.0", event: {"id":"66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2","type":"EXPIRATION","app_user_id":"user_1","product_id":"pro_monthly","expiration_reason":"BILLING_ERROR"} });
const t = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const header = `t=${t},v1=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex")}`;

const seen = new Set(); // use a database table in production

function handle(rawBody, header) {
  if (!verify(rawBody, header, secret)) return "401 bad signature";
  const { event } = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  if (seen.has(event.id)) return "200 duplicate";
  seen.add(event.id);
  if (event.type !== "EXPIRATION") return "200 ignored";
  return event.expiration_reason === "BILLING_ERROR" ? "remove access, ask for a new payment method" : "remove access, start win-back";
}

console.log(handle(rawBody, header));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `ask for a new payment method` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot produces it

A scheduled job (`services/tick.ts`) records `EXPIRATION` for every subscription whose access, grace period included, has ended, and claims each one once so replicas do not send it twice. The reason comes from the stored state: paused, then a billing issue, then the stored cancel reason, else `UNSUBSCRIBE`.

# What does the RevenueDot webhook event INITIAL_PURCHASE mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/webhooks/webhook-initial-purchase.md
Description: INITIAL_PURCHASE is sent when a customer first buys a subscription, including a free trial start. Grant access to the entitlements and record the customer.

The RevenueDot webhook event INITIAL_PURCHASE means a customer bought a subscription for the first time, including the start of a free trial.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Event | `INITIAL_PURCHASE` |
| Where | RevenueDot webhook (`event.type`), RevenueCat's webhook format |
| Sent to | Every enabled webhook whose filters match |
| Fields that are specific to it | none beyond the common subscription fields |
| What it means | The first purchase of a subscription, including a free trial start. |

## When it is sent

- A subscription chain that RevenueDot has not seen before is recorded, from the SDK, a store notification (when new purchases are tracked), an import or a web checkout.
- `period_type` is `TRIAL` for a free trial and `INTRO` for a paid introductory offer; `NORMAL` otherwise.
- It is sent once per chain. A lapsed customer who comes back gets `RENEWAL`, not a second `INITIAL_PURCHASE`.

## What your server should do

1. Grant the entitlements in `entitlement_ids` until `expiration_at_ms`.
2. Record `original_transaction_id` as the key for the whole subscription.
3. In a trial, do not count revenue yet: `price` is the money that moved, and is 0 for a free trial.
4. Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

## Example

```javascript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">
function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const m = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header ?? "");
  if (!m || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(m[1])) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${m[1]}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, Buffer.from(m[2], "hex"));
}

// Sign a sample delivery the way RevenueDot does, then handle it.
const secret = "whsec_test_secret";
const rawBody = JSON.stringify({ api_version: "1.0", event: {"id":"66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2","type":"INITIAL_PURCHASE","app_user_id":"user_1","product_id":"pro_monthly","period_type":"NORMAL","entitlement_ids":["pro"]} });
const t = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const header = `t=${t},v1=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex")}`;

const seen = new Set(); // use a database table in production

function handle(rawBody, header) {
  if (!verify(rawBody, header, secret)) return "401 bad signature";
  const { event } = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  if (seen.has(event.id)) return "200 duplicate";
  seen.add(event.id);
  if (event.type !== "INITIAL_PURCHASE") return "200 ignored";
  return "grant " + event.product_id + " until expiration_at_ms, record the customer";
}

console.log(handle(rawBody, header));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `grant pro_monthly` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot produces it

When a store change arrives for a chain RevenueDot has no stored purchase for, the diff in `diffSubscription` returns `INITIAL_PURCHASE` first. A refunded or already cancelled first purchase also gets a `CANCELLATION` right after it, and an outstanding price increase gets its consent event.

# What does the RevenueDot webhook event INVOICE_ISSUANCE mean?

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/revenuedot/docs/main/docs/webhooks/webhook-invoice-issuance.md
Description: INVOICE_ISSUANCE is accepted in a webhook filter but RevenueDot never sends it, because only RevenueCat Billing issues invoices.

The RevenueDot webhook event INVOICE_ISSUANCE is never sent, because RevenueDot does not issue invoices.

## Quick facts

| | |
|---|---|
| Event | `INVOICE_ISSUANCE` |
| Where | RevenueDot webhook (`event.type`), RevenueCat's webhook format |
| Sent to | No webhook: it is never sent |
| Fields that are specific to it | none |
| What it means | A RevenueCat event type for an invoice issued by RevenueCat Billing. RevenueDot accepts it in a webhook's `event_types` filter and never sends it. |

## When it is sent

- RevenueCat sends it when RevenueCat Billing issues an invoice.
- RevenueDot has no invoicing product, so nothing produces the event.
- A web checkout on Stripe sends Stripe's own invoice emails and events, not this one.

## What your server should do

1. Do not wait for this event.
2. If you migrate from RevenueCat and used it, take invoices from Stripe's own webhooks instead.
3. Keep a no-op case for it if you share a handler between both systems.
4. Deduplicate on `event.id`: deliveries can repeat, because anything but HTTP 200 is retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 minutes.

## Example

```javascript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

// X-RevenueCat-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">
function verify(rawBody, header, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const m = /^t=(\d+),v1=([0-9a-f]{64})$/.exec(header ?? "");
  if (!m || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(m[1])) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${m[1]}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(expected, Buffer.from(m[2], "hex"));
}

// Sign a sample delivery the way RevenueDot does, then handle it.
const secret = "whsec_test_secret";
const rawBody = JSON.stringify({ api_version: "1.0", event: {"id":"66339910-3BFF-49F4-B873-D1283D673DE2","type":"INVOICE_ISSUANCE","app_user_id":"user_1","product_id":"pro_monthly"} });
const t = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
const header = `t=${t},v1=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex")}`;

const seen = new Set(); // use a database table in production

function handle(rawBody, header) {
  if (!verify(rawBody, header, secret)) return "401 bad signature";
  const { event } = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  if (seen.has(event.id)) return "200 duplicate";
  seen.add(event.id);
  if (event.type !== "INVOICE_ISSUANCE") return "200 ignored";
  return "no-op, RevenueDot never sends this";
}

console.log(handle(rawBody, header));
```

*Run-checked: `npm run check:snippets` runs this snippet with Node and compares its output with `no-op` (checked 2026-10-03).*

## How RevenueDot produces it

The type is in `EVENT_TYPES` so a filter that names it is valid, and in `NEVER_SENT_EVENT_TYPES` so nothing produces it.
